events.title: Tropical Forest Panama
events.description: Embark on a spectacular journey through the lush vegetation and vibrant culture of Panama, the incredibly biodiverse land bridge connecting North and South America. Tropical Forest Panama invites guests to take an exciting, immersive journey to discover the nature, culture and interconnectedness of the forest system. Gorgeous greenery and flowers, engaging new interpretation stations and new live animal features are inspired by our Phipps staff members' journey to Darién National Park and subsequent research. Panama is a relatively small nation — about the size of South Carolina — with an outsized impact on the world. About 40% of all U.S. freight containers move through its famous canal. But Panama’s global importance dates back to long before the canal was built — and it's home to more species of birds, amphibians, reptiles and insects than the U.S. and Canada combined. Join us as we explore this one-of-a-kind place where people, plants and animals comprise a thriving ecosystem that constitutes one of the wildest places on Earth.

events.title: French Moderns: Matisse / Renoir / Degas
events.description: Immerse yourself in French Moderns: Matisse / Renoir / Degas, an exhibition of about 60 artworks that positions France as the artistic center of international Modernism from the mid-nineteenth to mid-twentieth centuries.Encompassing realism, impressionism, post-impressionism, symbolism, Fauvism, cubism, and surrealism, French Moderns: Matisse / Renoir / Degas exemplifies the avant-garde movements that defined modern art in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries and that continue to awe art-goers today. Ranging widely in style, the exhibition features paintings, drawings and sculptures created by the era’s leading artists born in France, as well as those who studied and exhibited there, including Paul Cézanne, Marc Chagall, Camille Corot, Gustave Courbet, Edgar Degas, Jean-Léon Gérôme, Henri Matisse, Berthe Morisot, Gabriele Münter, Pierre-Auguste Renoir, and Auguste Rodin.French Moderns: Matisse / Renoir / Degas is organized by Lisa Small, Senior Curator of European Art, and Richard Aste, former Curator of European Art at the Brooklyn Museum

events.title: Beauty of the Burgh Bike Tour
events.description: Join Bike the Burgh on an exploratory adventure of Downtown Pttsburgh. This tour is perfect if you are new to the city and you would like to see the most interesting spots of Pittsburgh- but if you know the Burgh already, we promise that you will still learn unknown historical facts!​On this tour we will cruise through the streets of the Financial and Cultural district, explore the Strip District and check out the North Shore on its scenic river trails. We will dive into the history of Pittsburgh, tracking down the people who shaped this city to what it is today: a beauty. events.title: The Football Town
events.description: As part of the celebration of Western Pennsylvania’s rich football history leading up to the 2026 NFL Draft in Pittsburgh, NFL Films presents the world premiere of “The Football Town,” which explores the region’s storied football tradition.The first-ever immersive format documentary produced by NFL Films will run throughout the weeks leading up to and following the 2026 NFL Draft taking place this April 23-25 in Pittsburgh. events.title: Intro to Forging Series with Danielle Brannigan
events.description: Discover the possibilities of working with ferrous and non-ferrous metals! 6-Week Series Date: Thursdays, September 24th – October 29th Time: 6pm – 9pm, each Thursday Description: Explore the possibilities of forging with copper, brass, and mild steel! Students will experiment with cold working, annealing, fold forming, air chasing, and surface development while learning how different metals respond to heat, force, and forming. Over six weeks, students will create individual projects, refine techniques, and develop the skills necessary to work with metal. Your instructor will provide demonstrations, open studio time, guidance, and feedback throughout the process, concluding with finishing and a group sharing of completed work! Students will learn studio safety, proper tool/equipment use, and walk away with new skills and feeling inspired! Students will leave with foundational skills in forging, forming, and working with copper, brass, and mild steel, along with individual pieces or studies exploring jewelry, sculpture, functional, or mixed-media applications. This class will involve hot metal, fire, and repetitive swinging of a hammer, it can be somewhat physically demanding at times, so slight stamina is recommended. Tuition: $330+ $60 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided. Students should wear natural fibers such as cotton and denim. Uncuffed pants and closed-toe shoes are required (no shorts or sandals permitted). Long hair should be restrained. Safety glasses and hearing protection are provided; however, participants may bring their own if preferred. We recommend bringing a water bottle to stay hydrated. This workshop is in an open air studio, bring a coat to keep warm before the forges get fired up! Location: Contemporary Craft – Timmons Studios, Blacksmithing Studio (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. ANY WORKSHOP OR INDIVIDUAL SESSION CANCELLATIONS WILL BE COMMUNICATED VIA EMAIL. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. We are unable to refund materials cost for this workshop. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Danielle Brannigan is a Pittsburgh-based silversmith, blacksmith, artist, and educator who works across jewelry, small- and large-scale sculpture, metal fabrication, and welding. She loves working with all forms of metal, with a particular affinity for steel and copper. Her practice is rooted in experimentation, hands-on making, and discovering new possibilities within the material. She has a special interest in reclaimed steel and recycled materials, giving new life to materials through transformation and reuse. In her current explorations, Danielle is experimenting with enameling steel, exploring the interplay of color, surface, texture, and form. As an educator, she encourages curiosity, experimentation, and a willingness to push the material in unexpected directions.

events.title: New & Noted: Ariel Lawhon
events.description: A sweeping historical adventure inspired by the life of Grace O’Malley, the legendary Irish folk heroine who risked everything to defend her people. Venture onto the high seas with the thrilling latest from the New York Times bestselling author of The Frozen River and I Was Anastasia.Grace O’Malley was born to be a sea captain. But despite her natural skill on the water, Grace learns early that her dreams of a life at the helm are not compatible with the expectations of her noble family. As the only daughter of a powerful chieftain, her role is to secure a strong alliance and bear children. But when she’s sent to foster with a nearby clan, Grace falls for a clever and open-minded second son—a man she cannot have.Married off against her will to a brutal warrior, Grace performs her duty, all the while gathering followers loyal to her, and consolidating her husband’s power, only to be ousted from his lands. But this betrayal offers Grace the opportunity to return to sea, finally leading clan O’Malley’s mighty fleet. Just as she finds true independence, Queen Elizabeth’s incursions into Ireland grow bolder and Grace must fight to defend her land, her ships, and the people she loves most against the cruel and power-hungry English deputies, who will stop at nothing to check her power.Keenly observed and fiercely written, Ariel Lawhon’s new action-packed novel channels the untamed beauty and harsh realities of sixteenth-century Ireland, as seen through the eyes of an unforgettable heroine who rightly became “the Pirate Queen of Ireland.”Ariel Lawhon is an award-winning, critically acclaimed, New York Times bestselling author of historical fiction. Her books have been translated into over thirty languages and have been Good Morning America, LibraryReads, and One Book One County selections. She lives in the rolling hills outside Nashville, Tennessee, with her husband and four sons. Ariel splits her time between the grocery store and the baseball field.

events.title: 2026 Backyard Docs Film Festival
events.description:
Backyard Docs Film Festival is an annual celebration of non-fiction cinema that explores our region’s Rust Belt and Appalachian identity.
The festival showcases documentary films and filmmakers directly connected to our region or that share our region’s identity and culture. Formerly known as The Rust Belt & Appalachia Documentary Film Festival, the Backyard Docs Film Festival continues its trademark DIY screening style, holding screenings in unconventional locations such as abandoned factories, dive bars, rooftops, and backyards. The four-day event will also feature a panel discussion with regional industry leaders in documentary and visual journalism, private rough-cut feedback sessions, professional development workshops with world-renowned filmmakers, and, of course, great afterparties. It’s the one time of year when filmmakers, journalists, and artists of all stripes can come together, build new connections, and help redefine the story of the Rust Belt and Appalachia.

The four-day event will also feature a panel discussion with regional industry leaders in documentary and visual journalism, private rough-cut feedback sessions, professional development workshops with world-renowned filmmakers, and, of course, great afterparties. It’s the one time of year when filmmakers, journalists, and artists of all stripes can come together, build new connections, and help redefine the story of the Rust Belt and Appalachia.

events.title: The Very First AND Longest Running Chicago Tribute Band In The World is Making A Tour Stop at The Palace Theatre September 24th
events.description: There are a lot of bands doing a tribute to the band Chicago, but back in the early 90s, when Powerhouse decided to put together their Chicago Transit tribute act, they were the first in the world to do so. And they remain “The First and Longest Running Chicago Tribute Band in the World” and the only one to carry five lead vocalists, just as the band Chicago does. Chicago Transit’s Chicago Tribute Show will come to The Palace Theatre Thursday, September 24th, 2026 at 7:30pm. You can even sing and dance along if you’d like. Tickets are just $35., $44., $49., and $75. and can be purchased online at: www.westmorelandculturaltrust.org or by calling the ticket office at (724) 836-8000. The Palace Theatre is located at 21 W. Otterman, Greensburg, PA 15601. This show is presented by Latshaw Productions. The bands’ 5 lead singers, the 3-piece horn section and the 5-piece rhythm section, made this show a natural for the band, even getting credit from the band Chicago themselves, back in the 90s. With the band’s three piece horn section, five piece rhythm section and five lead vocalists is able to cover all the Chicago material from the early horn-dominant classics like ‘Make Me Smile’, ’25 or 6 to 4’ and ‘Saturday in the Park’ to the later, softer, keyboard-oriented ballads like ‘If You Leave Me Now’. If you like Chicago, you’ll love Chicago Transit!

events.title: Textures of Being: Opening Reception
events.description: Join us for the opening reception of Textures of Being! Textures of Being is an exhibition which brings together artists whose practices honor the body—its sensitivities and its wisdom—as a site of deep creative knowledge. Rooted in materiality and lived experience, this exhibition reimagines disability as a form of freedom and a distinct intimate lens through which the world is encountered, shaped, and perceived. In the United States, one in four adults lives with a disability. Yet our environment and cultural system continue to privilege an imagined norm, often neglecting the rich variation of how bodies move, feel, perceive, and relate. This exhibition shifts the focus from compliance and accommodation to the sensory realities that animate disabled life—textures of resistance and adaptation, fragility and strength, constraint and imagination. Together, the artists create a multidimensional portrait of embodiment that exceeds symbolic inclusion and moves toward a fuller, more tender understanding of what it means to inhabit a body. The intimacy and solidarity expressed through the work evoke a sense of care, reciprocity and community. Textures of Being will be on view from September 25, 2026 – January 16, 2027. This exhibition was juried and organized by Yu-San Cheng, Director of Visual Engagement at Contemporary Craft, and Fran Ledonio Flaherty, the creator of Anthropology of Motherhood and a Deaf artist based in Pittsburgh.An ASL interpreter will be available for this event. If you wish to request further accessibility accommodations, please reach out to yscheng@contemporarycraft.org.This event is free and open to the public.

events.title: Joey Adams w/ Trey Johnston & Noah Collins
events.description: Doors 7pm | Show 8pm$12 ADV | $15 DOS21+Joey Adams - An Ohio native moved to West Virginia, Joey Adams combines both the rock n roll he grew up on with the Appalachian bluegrass hes come to love. Through the use of his sharp storytelling abilities, Adams crafts the lyrics of his songs to talk about his own experiences as well as others. From writing intense break up songs like Deep End to laid back ballads about home such as East Ohio, Adams continues to write relatable and meaningful songs.Trey Johnston - Born and raised in the outskirts of rural Ohio, Southern Rock and Country music have major influences on Treys songwriting style as well as musical accompaniment preferences. With a more modern twist on Southern Rock or Grunge Country music. Noah Collins - A Chattanooga native, Noah Collins lived in the Dominican Republic for twenty-four months. It was there in the campos where Collins says he developed his percussive finger picking style. 2007 brought him back home to begin work on his debut release Heart on a Line. Americana-UK gave the album 7 of 10 stars after its release in 2008.With coarse, heart-filled vocals comparable to Manchester-born musician David Gray and American songwriter Bob Dylan, Noah Collins delivers a moving performance. A compositional minimalist, Collins compliments simple words with discreet rhythms.

events.description: Back for year 7! What the F**k Was That? This hilarious show takes all the elements of the cult classic films The Evil Dead, Evil Dead 2, and Army of Darkness and combines them into one of the craziest theatrical experiences of all time. Five college students go to an abandoned cabin in the woods and accidentally unleash an evil force that turns them all into demons. It's all up to Ash (a housewares employee turned demon-killing hero) and his trusty chainsaw to save the day.Blood flies. Limbs are dismembered. Demons tell bad jokes... and all to music. The songs in the show are completely off the wall. Titles like "All the Men in My Life Keep Getting Killed by Candarian Demons" and "What the F**k Was That?" will have audiences rolling in their seats and screaming for more and more blood.

It's all up to Ash (a housewares employee turned demon-killing hero) and his trusty chainsaw to save the day.Blood flies. Limbs are dismembered. Demons tell bad jokes... and all to music. The songs in the show are completely off the wall. Titles like "All the Men in My Life Keep Getting Killed by Candarian Demons" and "What the F**k Was That?" will have audiences rolling in their seats and screaming for more and more blood.

events.title: Pittsburgh Panthers Football
events.description: Pittsburgh Panthers football is the college football program representing the University of Pittsburgh, known for its rich history, passionate fanbase, and long-standing tradition within major college athletics. The Panthers have produced numerous legendary players, championship seasons, and memorable moments that helped shape the history of college football. Playing home games at Acrisure Stadium, the program is recognized for intense rivalries, strong defensive traditions, and a proud connection to Pittsburgh’s blue-collar sports culture. With a legacy that includes national championships, Hall of Fame talent, and decades of competitive success, Pittsburgh Panthers football remains one of the most respected programs in collegiate athletics.

events.title: Patriots 5K
events.address: 10301 Pearce Mill Rd, Allison Park, Pennsylvania 15101
events.description: Get ready for an inspiring day at the inaugural Patriots 5K on Saturday, September 26, 2026, taking place at the picturesque North Park Boathouse in Allison Park, Allegheny. This vibrant event invites everyone—whether you choose to run, walk, or ruck—to join in honoring the brave lives of our nation's veterans and supporting military families. The scenic 5K course offers participants a chance to stand in solidarity with those who have served and the families who carry their legacies forward.This special occasion also marks the launch of Semper Fi Mission's White Star Initiative, which aims to provide scholarships and support for children who have lost a parent to veteran suicide. Event highlights include a timed 5K run/walk/ruck, a Veterans Resource Fair, and a heartfelt remembrance ceremony honoring veterans we have lost. By participating, you are not only celebrating our heroes but also making a meaningful impact in the lives of veterans and families in crisis throughout Western Pennsylvania. Come together with your community to Run. Remember. Honor.

events.title: Homestead 1892: Exploring the Lockout and Strike with The Frick Pittsburgh and Rivers of Steel
events.description: Co-presented by The Frick Pittsburgh and Rivers of Steel, this special program investigates the lasting impact of the 1892 Homestead Lockout and Strike, 134 years after that fateful July. Begin the morning with an exploration of the Pump House, a rare access experience to discuss the events of July 1892, including the deadly conflict between workers and Pinkerton agents, followed by a guided tour of Carrie Blast Furnace to understand the realities of the Pittsburgh steel and iron industries. Next, travel to The Frick Pittsburgh for a deeper investigation of Henry Clay Frick’s relationship to labor and his decisions during that summer on a custom tour of Clayton.Advanced registration and pre-payment required. Program begins at the Pump House, 880 E. Waterfront Drive, Munhall PA 15120; participants are responsible for their own transportation. Registration includes admission to Carrie Blast Furnace, the Pump House, and Clayton, as well as a boxed lunch.Program Schedule (times are approximate):9:30-10:30 am – Tour of The Pump House10:30-10:40 am – Travel to Carrie Blast Furnace10:40-12:00 pm – Tour of Carrie Blast Furnace12:00-12:15 pm – Depart for the Frick12:15-1:00 pm – Lunch at the Frick1:00-2:30 pm – Tour Clayton

events.title: 30th Anniversary Mavuno: A Pearl of the Community
events.description: 30th Anniversary Mavuno: A Pearl of the Community30 Years of Grit, Grace, and GratitudeCelebrating three decades in Sewickley, the Mavuno Festival honors the creativity, leadership, and cultural contributions of Black artists and educators. Meaning “harvest” in Swahili, Mavuno reflects a legacy of community, culture, and artistic growth.This milestone year explores themes of grit, grace, and gratitude—highlighting resilience, cultural identity, and the beauty that emerges through challenge and growth. The festival also proudly celebrates and uplifts local Black and BIPOC-owned businesses, recognizing their vital role in sustaining culture, community, and economic empowerment.Mavuno focuses on an annual festival featuring local art vendors, live music, and food, as well as an art exhibition in Sweetwater’s gallery. The festival has grown to include a beer garden in recent years, as we continue to expand and build community partnerships. Mavuno aims to celebrate BIPOC artists, amplify voices, and create a platform for small businesses and artisans.Walnut Street will close from Duquesne Way to Thorn Street to allow for vendors, live music, a beer garden, and all festival activities!

events.title: Introduction to Blacksmithing
events.description: Blacksmithing classes at Old Economy Village offer a unique and immersive experience for adults eager to explore the rich history of metalworking. Set in a meticulously reconstructed 19th-century smithy, these classes provide an authentic glimpse into the life and craft of blacksmiths from a bygone era. Participants will learn traditional forging techniques using tools and methods that have stood the test of time.Ideal for beginners, the introductory classes focus on the essential skills needed to work with hot metal, including heating, hammering, bending, and twisting. Under the guidance of experienced instructors, students will complete a hands-on project by crafting a decorative S-hook—a classic piece that demonstrates both utility and artistry. Whether you're a history enthusiast, a craftsperson at heart, or simply curious about the trade, these classes offer a rare opportunity to step back in time and connect with an age-old craft.Participants must be 18+

Under the guidance of experienced instructors, students will complete a hands-on project by crafting a decorative S-hook—a classic piece that demonstrates both utility and artistry. Whether you're a history enthusiast, a craftsperson at heart, or simply curious about the trade, these classes offer a rare opportunity to step back in time and connect with an age-old craft.Participants must be 18+

events.title: 60th Royal American Regiment and Garrison at the Fort!
events.description: Meet members of the 60th Royal American Regiment as they garrison at the Fort this weekend.After General Braddock’s defeat at the Battle of the Monongahela in 1755, the British Crown authorized the raising of a regiment of four battalions for service in North America. Recruited in Germany and among the Swiss and German settlers of Pennsylvania, Maryland, and Virginia, this regiment eventually became the the 60th or Royal American Regiment of Foot. The various battalions played a major role in nearly every campaign of the French and Indian War (1755-63) and Pontiac’s War (1763-64).History Alive! at Fort Ligonier is an engaging experience for visitors to learn more about the daily life of a frontier military outpost in North America during the 18th century. Through daily programming depicting typical activities of a military site such as soldiering, manual labor, tailoring, laundry, and cooking, and special weekend demonstrations from 18th century artisans, History Alive! portrays the people who fought and lived at Fort Ligonier during the Forbes Campaign of 1758.This educational program is made possible by a #PreservingAmerica grant from Americana Corner.

events.title: Introduction to Improv Embroidery with Alison Stein
events.description: Create an improvisational embroidery piece, taking a "doodle approach" to stitches! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, September 26 Time: 2 – 5 pm Description: This workshop will provide gentle encouragement and instruction on how to create beautiful embroidery pieces using an unplanned, improvisational approach. Whether you have never picked up a needle or are an experienced embroiderer, this method is available to you. Enjoy the beauty of color, textile and fiber without any stress of “messing up,” which is simply impossible in this approach! Techniques and Skills covered in this class will include: Learning (or unlearning) the mindset of embroidery without a pattern. Sourcing, selecting and preparing fabric and fiber for improv embroidery. Taking a “doodle approach” to embroidery stitches. We will take a different approach to learning or re-learning the basic embroidery stitches, encouraging beginners to feel confident, and more advanced students will have a new way of thinking about and building on stitches they already know. Thinking about color choices and composition Methods for addressing results you don’t love. Tuition: $65 + $15 materials fee Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available-with some limitations- to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Fill out the scholarship application here , and you can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Materials: All materials will be provided, however, participants are encouraged to bring any tools that they need to aid in seeing up-close: reading glasses, magnifyers, etc… Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Alison J. Stein is an artist, teacher and writer based in Carnegie, PA, in the Pittsburgh metro area. She makes vibrant textile art, paintings, prints and book art, and enjoys blurring the boundaries between traditional techniques and contemporary art.

events.description: Join Walk the Burgh and make new friends! Meet other beer lovers on this brewery tour while sampling a variety of locally crafted brews. Stroll through one of the most vibrant neighborhoods of Pittsburgh and learn all about the history of beer making in Pittsburgh and Western PA. events.title: Whiskey Rebellion & Prohibition Walking Tour
events.description: Our cocktail tour! From the mill to the still, whiskey has been a cornerstone in Pittsburgh's history. Come downtown for our whiskey tour where you will discover how whiskey has fueled political, labor and social movements throughout the region. Begin and end your tour in style with a Prohibition cocktail at the Ritual House and an Old Fashioned at the Rebel Room. As we walk the streets of Downtown, along iconic architecture, you'll learn about the violent Whiskey Rebellion in Pittsburgh, hidden former (as well as existing!) speakeasies around the city, and how Prohibition affected the region. events.title: Jim Hensons Labyrinth in Concert
events.description: Jim Henson’s Labyrinth in Concert is a live cinematic event that combines a screening of the beloved fantasy film Labyrinth with musicians performing the movie’s iconic soundtrack in sync with the film. Originally released in the 1980s, Labyrinth became a cult classic through its imaginative storytelling, elaborate puppetry, fantasy world-building, and memorable performance by David Bowie as the Goblin King. The concert experience enhances the film’s magical atmosphere by bringing its music to life through live instrumentation and immersive theatrical energy. Blending nostalgia, fantasy adventure, and live performance, Jim Henson’s Labyrinth in Concert offers audiences a unique celebration of one of fantasy cinema’s most enduring cult favorites.

The production incorporates a multimedia presentation and high-energy performance style modeled on Def Leppard’s 1980s arena shows.

events.title: SkyWatch: Discovering Planets
events.description: Celebrate Neptune’s discovery with us! In September 1846, Neptune became the first planet located through mathematical predictions rather than through regular observations of the sky. Explore methods used to discover both solar system planets and exoplanets through two immersive activities investigating hidden object shadows and phenomena like stellar wobble and planet formation. The night also includes a planetarium show and time to explore the night sky from the observatory deck (weather-permitting). Viewing objects include Saturn, the Moon, and binary star Albireo A and B.

events.description: Introducing Denny Love, a Los Angeles–based actor and comedian whose career seamlessly bridges prestige television, live comedy, and viral digital culture. A celebrated alumnus of DePaul University’s renowned Theatre School, Denny first broke through with a standout performance in Hulu’s Looking for Alaska, a critically acclaimed series boasting a 92% Rotten Tomatoes rating. He went on to appear in two seasons of Taylor Sheridan’s hit Paramount+ drama Mayor of Kingstown, further solidifying his dramatic range. Why'd We Book It? Denny Love has been an exciting new voice in comedy and we have been fans since seeing him on Mayor of Kingstown. His crowd work is always a pleasure to see pop up on the feed. For Fans Of... Kevin Langue, Trevor Wallace, Shapel Lacey Extended Bio: Beyond the screen, Denny is a commanding live performer who has shared stages with comedy heavyweights and delivered memorable sets opening for Theo Von. As a key cast member of @KevinLangue’s viral YouTube and TikTok content, he has helped build a digital powerhouse of over 4.47 million subscribers and more than 2 billion views worldwide. In 2026, he takes the stage at Netflix Is a Joke, solidifying his place among the most sought-after rising voices in entertainment. This summer, he joins the Kevin Langue Show as a key performer on an ambitious 18- city national theatre tour, bringing his sharp timing and undeniable charisma to audiences across the country. Building on that momentum, Denny will launch his first headlining tour in Fall 2026, marking a major milestone as he steps fully into his own spotlight. **Disclaimer: Adult subject matter** Seating/Show Information: Limit 6 tickets per transaction. The time listed on the ticket is the event's true start time. Most shows have a preshow experience starting 1 hour before the show. All tickets are non-refundable - our full refund policy can be viewed here Please contact us ahead of time with any accesibilty requests or concerns, we're happy to accomodate you. events.title: Decade Shifter
events.description:
Decade Shifter
Date: September 26, 2026

Time: 9:00 PM – 4:00 AM

Tickets: $20 / $25

Admission: 21+

stress tess (@stress.tess)

stress tess is a Brooklyn-based DJ exploring the hypnotic edges of techno and psychedelic dance music. Her long-form sets move patiently through shimmering minimalism, pulsing rhythms, and deep groove, creating immersive soundscapes that invite listeners inward. She is a founding member of Vortex, the collective behind Area X, a New York party series devoted to cultivating intimate dance floors and expansive states of listening.

dj33L (@dj_33l)


dj33L is a DJ and organizer based in NYC. A product of Brooklyn’s DIY music scene, he seeks to contribute more ways in which we can hold space for each other and advance our shared journey of understanding and self discovery. dj33L is drawn to hypnotic and minimal techno as the foundation of his sound, also shaped by hardgroove and punk influences. This manifests as warmth, spaciousness, and intrigue in thoughtful narrative arcs.

Formosa

Formosa is a multidisciplinary Taiwanese-American DJ, artist, and designer who performs as "formosa" and as half of regular Pittsburgh queer party and music duo, Jellyfish. Behind the decks from Pittsburgh to New York, Toronto, London, Mexico, and Taipei, you can expect their sets to range from driving italo to electro, acid house, drum and bass, breakbeat, minimal, and more. Formosa will take you on a journey through driving bass lines and syncopated rhythms, sprinkled with playful melodies. You can catch their sets on SoundCloud, at any Jellyfish party, and at your local discotheque.

nonsite

nonsite is a local hardware techno producer.

Martingale

Bubbling and growling hypnotic and energetic techno.

events.title: Abandon All Hope: Through the Gates of Hell with Dante and Rodin
events.description: Join Dr. Kahren Jones Arbitman for an exploration of Auguste Rodin's spectacular creation: The Gates of Hell.“Abandon All Hope Ye Who Enter Here.” Not exactly the welcome one might expect when arriving at a Parisian public institution. And yet, this terrifying phrase provided the creative spark for August Rodin’s spectacular creation, The Gates of Hell, slated for the façade of a new museum. Initially inspired by Dante’s Inferno and enhanced by later artistic and written descriptions of “Hellfire and brimstone,” Rodin poured his creative spirit into a project that would last twenty years. Hundreds of changes followed year after year as a final version took shape. The result was unlike anything the world had ever seen. Sadly, Rodin would never see it cast in bronze, much less installed as a museum portal. Its story is one of art history’s most frustrating tales where one man’s genius runs headlong into mind-numbing bureaucracy.Beginning with Dante’s Inferno, this lecture will usher the audience pictorially through the bowels of Hell where eternal torment awaits. When ultimately arriving at the foot of Rodin’s majestic gates, exhilaration replaces all sense of dread. Come for the torment, stay for the bliss.

events.title: The Summer Slow Down - Yoga Workshop
events.description: Slowing down is not a luxury; it is a return to your natural rhythm. In this workshop we are practicing the radical art of undoing by using restorative yoga + yoga nidra to improve our mental acuity and deepen into a state of relaxation. When the body feels safe and supported, the parasympathetic nervous system turns on, allowing for healing at every level. May this practice remind you that to pause is the most productive thing you can do.The importance of rest has and will always be a corner stone in our physical well-being. In this workshop you will explore postures that activate the parasympathetic state of “rest and digest”. The practice of restorative yoga will help to counter the effects of stress, burn out and busyness our lives. You will be guided in to several postures using the support of props to create safety in the body enabling you to let go followed by a guided meditation know as yoga nidra allowing you to relax into a deeply meditative state. All are welcome to join this practice of deep rest.

events.title: The Summer Slow Down with Cass
events.description: The summer slow down is your invitation to take a big energetic exhale and pause before going into the next season. As we conclude one of the busiest times of year filled with picnics, parties and celebrations you’re invited to pause. In a culture, where constant striving is the norm the summer slow down is the antidote to busyness, burn out. This is an opportunity to refresh mental acuity and physically rest.  We will enter restorative yoga postures that transport you into a savasana state. The shapes are supported by props to create a gentle opening rather than deep stretching.

events.title: Bear Ghost
events.description: Bear Ghost is a Phoenix-based “Adventure Rock” band known for blending playful musicianship, complex melodies, layered harmonies, heavy riffs, and pop-minded song structures. Their theatrical, genre-bending sound pairs energetic rock performances with an imaginative sense of humor, creating an inviting experience for listeners who enjoy music that is both technically inventive and unabashedly fun. The band’s live background includes festival appearances and support slots for artists such as Closure in Moscow, KONGOS, Brick + Mortar, and Okilly Dokilly. Expect a lively, unconventional concert from a group that brings personality and showmanship to every song.

events.title: Spotlight: September LGTBQ+ Theatre Jam Session
events.description: Join us for the next in-person monthly jam session for Spotlight, a space for Pittsburgh-based LGBTQ+ theatre artists to take center stage. During these meet-ups, we invite LGBTQ+ folx of all backgrounds and experience levels to share their talents and ideas with each other in a fun and casual atmosphere. If you’re an actor and have a monologue that needs an audience, come on down and let it rip. If you’re a playwright and have 5-10 pages of a play you’ve been working on, bring them over and let’s read them. If you’re a designer and have a design concept you’re dying to share with some fellow artists, we’d love to hear all about it. If you want to just observe and cheer on, awesome! Any and all theatre folk are welcome to the party.Reservations are required. Please email lgbtburghspotlight@gmail.com and send us the following info by September 25th:• Your name• Your pronouns• How you’d like to participate (if you’d like to share a monologue, song, scene, design work; just tell us a little about who you are; or simply observe)We can’t wait to see you there!When: September 27th, 7-9 pmWhere: Benedum Center 7th Floor Conference Room719 Liberty AvenuePittsburgh, PA 15222

events.title: Jay Buchanan
events.description: Jay Buchanan is the commanding vocalist and lyricist best known as the frontman of Grammy-nominated rock band Rival Sons. His solo performances showcase a more intimate side of his artistry, blending soulful vocals, country-rock storytelling, Southern gothic atmosphere and gospel-inspired feeling. Buchanan’s debut solo album, Weapons of Beauty, is out now and introduces a deeply personal creative direction shaped by widescreen narratives and richly textured roots music. Audiences can expect a compelling performance from a distinctive modern rock singer whose powerful voice and expressive songwriting remain at the center of every set.

events.address: 1495 Mercer Rd, Ellwood City, PA 16117, Ellwood City, Pennsylvania 16117
events.description: We invite you to tee up for a great cause at the St. Anthony School Programs Annual Golf Outing on Monday, September 28, at Olde Stonewall Golf Club. Whether you're aiming for a hole-in-one or simply looking to enjoy a beautiful day on the course, we hope you'll join us for a memorable day of golf, friendship, and philanthropy. Most importantly, all proceeds will go directly to the students and families served by St. Anthony School Programs. Registration and breakfast will begin at 7:00 a.m., followed by a shotgun start at 9:00 a.m. The scramble-format tournament will conclude with lunch and fellowship after play. For more than 70 years, St. Anthony School Programs has been helping students with Down syndrome, Autism Spectrum Disorder, and other special needs reach their full potential academically, socially, vocationally, and spiritually. Serving students ages 5–22 within select Catholic schools throughout the Pittsburgh region, our inclusive educational model provides opportunities for students of all faiths to learn, grow, and thrive. By joining us on the course, you'll help ensure that our students continue to have access to the specialized support and opportunities they need to succeed. It's a day where every drive, putt, and birdie helps move our mission forward. Singles, foursomes + sponsorships available!

events.title: Gogol Bordello
events.description: Gogol Bordello is an internationally acclaimed punk band known for its explosive fusion of punk rock, Eastern European folk music, ska, dub, and world music influences. Led by charismatic frontman Eugene Hütz, the group has built a reputation for high-energy performances that combine theatrical showmanship, cultural celebration, and infectious rhythms. Their music often explores themes of immigration, identity, freedom, resilience, and global unity while drawing inspiration from diverse musical traditions. Known for transforming concerts into vibrant celebrations filled with dancing, audience participation, and boundless energy, Gogol Bordello remains one of the most distinctive and exciting acts in alternative music.

events.title: Pure Prairie League
events.description: Pure Prairie League is a pioneering country-rock band formed in Ohio in the early 1970s. Best known for “Amie,” the enduring song from their album Bustin’ Out, the group also scored notable hits with “Let Me Love You Tonight” and “I’m Almost Ready.” Their long-running legacy includes Two Lane Highway, collaborations with artists such as Chet Atkins and Emmylou Harris, and a past lineup featuring future country star Vince Gill. Pure Prairie League continues its country-rock tradition with the album Back on Track.

events.title: Papermaking Series with Katy DeMent
events.description: Learn to utilize tools, materials, and processes of making your own paper ! (photo credit: Nathan Shaulis) 6-Week Series Date: Tuesdays, September 29 – November 3, 2026 Time: 5:30pm-8:30pm Description: Katy will share her decades of experience and deep knoweldge of histories, fibers, tools, processes, and joys of papermaking. Throughout the series, you can expect a full and comprehensive introduction to processes of creating paper. This series will introduce you to how to use the Contemporary Craft’s hollander paper beater, a tool for turning fibers into pulp. You will also learn to work with dyed pulps, as well as create collages by adding elements directly into your paper before it dries. The series will cover the following topics (schedule is subject to change): Week 1 “101” Papermaking introduction and Western sheet forming Week 2 “Color” Pulp painting with colorful dyed pulps Week 3 “Texture” Adding texture and random inclusions Week 4 “Plants” Paper straight from plants! Week 5 “Collage” Handmade Paper: Wet on wet collage Week 6: “Wet Bound Books!” Handmade paper books Tuition: $270 + $40 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided Registration: Register through Eventbrite. If you are viewing this listing on the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: We really want you to join us in the studio! Partial and full scholarships are available—with some limitations—to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist ” For my entire life I have been a working artist, organic gardener, and beekeeper. I create handmade paper as a means to an end. Paper art works take the form of: art lighting, shadow box, stationary, books and sculptures all crafted from sustainably collected plants, recycled and invasive fibers. Each piece is a vignette that holds a visual narrative. Through layers of vintage ephemera, photos and bits of cloth, tales are told. When etched images are included the dialogue begins. Toys, natural and found objects punctuate the story. No material is arbitrary; I am influenced by overlooked materials found in my community, my own back yard. Rusty old tools are mashed together with deconstructed plants; this is where I find humor, combining these unlikely fellows. Often my works invite the viewer to playfully interact with the art work through light and kinetic elements that bring the imagery to life.” – Katy DeMent

events.title: World of Music: Las Áñez (Colombian Folk, Pop & Electronic Fusion)
events.description:
Prepare to be hypnotized by the musical stylings of sibling duo Las Áñez. The Áñez twins’ music is designed to be performed live with a loop pedal and small instruments, in a minimal yet enchanting concert style. Their shows include songs from their four award-winning albums, which have captivated audiences in ten countries across the Americas and Europe with their unique blend of folklore and the avant-garde. 
This program is presented as a part of Songs in the Key of She, a new concert series taking place in Chicago, New York, and Pittsburgh that features and celebrates women musicians and composers from around the world. Produced by the Chicago-based nonprofit Torito Arts in collaboration with City of Asylum, the series aims to combat the underrepresentation of female musicians in the male-dominated music industry. Songs in the Key of She is a platform in which talented women in music share their creativity and stories with new audiences. 

This engagement of Las Áñez is made possible in part through the Performing Arts Global Exchange program of Mid Atlantic Arts. 

About the Artist:

The Áñez sisters are Juanita and Valentina Añez Rothmann. Both sisters sing on all their songs, half of which are composed and arranged by each of them, and they are the producers of their first three albums. Juanita plays the cuatro and percussion, and Valentina is a pianist and percussionist. Their albums include Silbidos (2017), Al Aire (2017), Reflexión (2020), Paralelas (2023), and, most recently, Duálismo Magico (2026).

About Your Visit: 
The in-house restaurant, Cucina Alfabeto, is open for dinner from 5 to 10 p.m. Please visit OpenTable (https://www.opentable.com/r/alfabeto-pittsburgh) or call 412-435-1111 to make a reservation.

events.title: Lunch Pail Lecture: The Women Behind the Walls of the French Nationality Room
events.description: Joanna Conings, Ph.D. candidate at the University of Pittsburgh uncovers and discusses the hidden labor and “affective diplomacies” through which women made the French Nationality Room at the University of Pittsburgh a reality, as evidenced in the University Archives at the University of Pittsburgh Library System. Hear stories of the inception of the room that has represented French culture and community in Pittsburgh for almost a century. Conings will guide attendees to reconsider how personal agency and affective diplomacy shape, and are shaped by, our shared architectural legacies.

events.title: Words & Pictures: Marley Dias
events.description: From global changemaker Marley Dias comes her picture book debut, I Am the Dream Come True, a resonant look at generational sacrifice and appreciation. Marley is best known for starting the famed #1000BlackGirlBooks campaign as a 6th grader, a collection of children’s books that feature Black girls as protagonists. She saw the issue of a lack of representation in kids lit and sought to make a change. This brought her national recognition and began her journey as a literacy advocate where she has received numerous accolades.In I Am the Dream Come True, Marley reflects on legacy, family, and gratitude—showing young readers how the hopes, sacrifices, and love of previous generations live on through them. Written in collaboration with her parents, Dr. Janice Johnson Dias and Scott Dias, the book is both an ode to ancestry and an empowering message for children: you are the dream your family believed in. It’s heartfelt, affirming, and ideal for conversations about Black identity, heritage, and family history.Marley Dias made headlines as a sixth grader when she started the #1000BlackGirlBooks campaign to collect children’s books featuring Black protagonists. Her initiative led to national media attention and served as a springboard to Marley’s global literacy advocacy work and social activism. Her book Marley Dias Gets It Done: And So Can You! was hailed in a Kirkus Reviews starred review as “an irresistible call to action for people of all ages.” Marley is currently the Ambassador of National Educational Association (NEA) Read Across America and serves as Host and Executive Producer of Netflix’s Bookmarks: Celebrating Black Voices. Marley is a graduate of Harvard University, where she earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Sociology. The Dias family lives in New Jersey. To learn more, visit marleydias.com/about.Dr. Janice Johnson Dias is the mother of Marley Dias and the founder and leader of GrassROOTS Community Foundation (GCF), where she trains girls to become trailblazers. Additionally, she is a renowned sociologist who has devoted her life to bridging the gap among research, theory, and practices. Dr. Johnson Dias is the author of Parent Like it Matters: How to Raise Joyful Change-Making Girls. The Dias family lives in New Jersey. To learn more, visit thedrjanice.com.Scott Dias is the father of Marley Dias, a real estate analytical geographer, and one of the key inspirations behind I Am the Dream Come True. The Dias family lives in New Jersey.

Together, Role Model and Samia offer a compelling showcase of modern songwriting, blending indie-pop and alternative influences into a concert experience filled with memorable melodies, emotional depth, and genuine artistic expression.

events.title: Calliope Presents Alla Boara
events.description: Working from Alan Lomax’s extraordinary 1954 field recordings of Italian regional folk songs, Alla Boara creates something vibrant and contemporary by suffusing the original source material with modern jazz sensibilities and global influences, creating a unique sound rooted in tradition but facing the future.Alla Boara celebrates the deep history of human music-making by cultivating fresh sounds from the ancient roots of regional Italian folk songs. The band’s captivating delivery is propelled by drummer Anthony Taddeo’s dynamic compositions, “breathing new possibilities into timeless stories while weaving in limitless and unexpected musical flavors” (Becca Stevens, GRAMMY-nominated singer/ songwriter).From the specific dialects, stories, and songs of Italy’s preindustrial past spring Alla Boara’s universally touching performances, which inspire listeners of any heritage to treasure their ancestral roots and to revel in our shared humanity – as surprising, playful, mournful, and tender as the songs themselves.

events.title: Jenny Owen Youngs and Northcote
events.description: Doors 7PM | Show 8PM $20 ADV | $25 DOSJenny Owens Young with her exceptional new Yep Roc debut, Avalanche, Youngs delivers a main course worthy of the wait. Written with a series of friends including S. Carey, Madi Diaz, The Antlers Peter Silberman, and Christian Lee Hutson and recorded with producer Josh Kaufman (Bonny Light Horseman, The Hold Steady, Cassandra Jenkins, Josh Ritter), the collection is an achingly beautiful exploration of loss, resilience, and growth from an artist whos experienced more than her fair share of each in recent years.Theres a good deal of heartbreak and disappointment in this music, Youngs explains, but it ultimately gives way to excitement and promise, to the incredible, immeasurable bliss of falling in love and finding yourself again. These songs travel the whole emotional spectrum.That kind of range has been Youngs calling card from the very start. Born and raised in rural New Jersey, she fell in love with The Beatles at an early age before eventually finding her way to The Cranberries and Elliott Smith in high school. Her self-recorded debut, Batten Down The Hatches, landed a high-profile sync in the Showtime series Weeds and led to a deal with Nettwerk Records, which re-released the album along with her 2009 follow-up, Transmitter Failure. Widespread acclaim and dates with the likes of Regina Spektor, Ingrid Michaelson, Frank Turner, and Aimee Mann followed, but by the time Youngs released her third album, 2012s An Unwavering Band Of Light, she was ready for a change of pace, moving to LA to focus on writing for other artists and for film and TV. In 2016, Youngs co-wrote Pitbulls Bad Man, which debuted at the 58th annual Grammy Awards; in 2017, she co-wrote Shungudzos Come On Back, which was featured in the Fifty Shades Freed soundtrack; and in 2018, she co-wrote Panic! At The Discos smash hit High Hopes, which went five-times platinum and broke the record for most weeks atop Billboards Hot Rock Songs chart. Along the way, Youngs also launched Buffering The Vampire Slayer, an episode-by-episode podcast devoted to Buffy The Vampire Slayer that attracted more than 160,000 monthly listeners and led to a book deal with St. Martins Press. Youngs recently launched a new series with her podcasting partner/ex-wife called The eX-Files and has a narrative fiction podcast due out next year, as well.Northcote brings a powerful, resonant acoustic performance rooted in honesty, grit, andemotional depth. His voice carries a rare warmth equal parts weathered and hopeful and his songs land with the weight of lived experience. Expect a set that feelspersonal, grounded, and deeply moving.

events.title: Odyssey Day
events.venue_name: Community College of Allegheny County - West Hills Center
events.description: Odyssey Day is a family-friendly educational event dedicated to promoting the use of clean, alternative fuels and advanced technology vehicles. The event provides the largest exhibit of alternative-fueled vehicles in Western Pennsylvania annually. Originally coordinated by the National Alternative Fuels Training Consortium (NAFTC) headquartered at West Virginia University in Morgantown, West Virginia, the event is now hosted each year by Pittsburgh Region Clean Cities (PRCC), a U.S. Department of Energy designated coalition in the Clean Cities and Communities partnership, a network of over 75 coalitions nationwide that are committed to lowering greenhouse gas emissions in the transportation sector through the use of clean fuels and alternate transport modalities. The event features panel presentations and guest speakers, a networking luncheon, a large alternative-fueled and electric vehicles display, a vendor networking fair, ice cream and more!

events.title: PGX 2026 - Pittsburgh Gaming Expo
events.description:
Pittsburgh Gaming Expo (PGX) 2026 returns October 2–4, 2026, bringing together gaming, tabletop, and geek culture alongside an impressive lineup of musical guests.

Headlining the music programming is POWERGLOVE, the legendary metal band known for their heavy metal covers of video game and pop culture themes (powerglovemusic.bandcamp.com). Also featured is LORDS OF THE TRIDENT, a high-energy power metal band from Madison, WI known for epic performances and elaborate stage theatrics (lordsofthetrident.bandcamp.com).

ARCADIA brings their unique 'Mario Kart Jazz!' experience to the expo — a jazz ensemble performing video game music arrangements. Joining them is KATIE SHESKO on flute, adding a classical touch to the gaming music celebration.

The expo also features a special DUNGEON SYNTH LOUNGE showcasing:
- FOGLORD – atmospheric dungeon synth artist (foglord.bandcamp.com)
- HILLSFAR – dungeon synth project with a fantasy RPG aesthetic
- JENN TAIGA – dark/extreme dungeon synth

PGX is held annually in Pittsburgh, PA and celebrates all things gaming — video games, tabletop RPGs, board games, card games, and geek culture — combined with live music and entertainment.

events.title: Shane Patrick in The Oracle
events.description: The Oracle is an immersive, story‑driven 75‑minute theatrical experience that blurs the line between history, illusion, and the supernatural. Audiences are transported back to early 1900s Vaudeville to witness the recreation of the infamous Oracle Act, headlined by Illiana, a young gypsy fortune teller who captivated vaudeville crowds with her uncanny ability to read minds and see the future.Her story ended in tragedy when she was found hanging from the rafters of a theatre at the height of her fame. Tonight, her act is reborn—and her spirit invited to speak once more.Shane Patrick is a professional mentalist and theatrical performer whose work blends mind reading, storytelling, and immersive theatre. For more than a decade, he has performed across the United States for audiences ranging from Fortune 100 companies to intimate theatre crowds. His performances explore the strange intersection between psychology, intuition, and the unexplained.The Oracle marks his most theatrical work to date—an atmospheric recreation of a mysterious vaudeville mind‑reading act said to have shocked audiences more than a century ago.

His performances are driven by soulful guitar work, improvisational intensity, and emotionally charged compositions that have inspired generations of rock musicians. events.title: Fastball
events.description: Fastball is an Austin, Texas, alternative-rock trio formed by Tony Scalzo, Miles Zuniga and Joey Shuffield. The band broke through with its platinum 1998 album, All the Pain Money Can Buy, which produced the signature hit “The Way,” along with “Out of My Head” and “Fire Escape.” Fastball earned two Grammy nominations in 1999, including Rock Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals for “The Way.” Known for melodic songwriting, harmony-rich vocals and concise pop-rock arrangements, the group has continued recording and performing across a catalog that includes The Harsh Light of Day, Keep Your Wig On and Step Into Light.

events.title: F*cktoys
events.description:
o-presented by the Harris Theater and Signal Otter Films with assistance from Pittsburgh Sound + Image, we bring you a one night only screening of F-Toys with writer, director, producer, and star Annapurna Sriram in person!

Friday, Oct 2 at 7:30 | Harris Theater | 809 Liberty Ave, Pittsburgh, PA

Directed by Annapurna Sriram

2025 | USA | English language | DCP

Part-time sex worker, full-time chaos magnet, AP is convinced that the universe has it out for her… and she might be right. In F-Toys — the wild, unfiltered debut from writer/director/star Annapurna Sriram — AP seeks a cosmic reset after a swampy tarot reading (courtesy Big Freedia) tells her she needs $1,000 and a sacrificial lamb to lift her curse. Armed with neither, she sets off on a bizarre quest with her kindred spirit Danni (Sadie Scott) through Trashtown, USA — a dystopian, neon-drenched sprawl of assorted oddballs, Tom of Finland cops, and strip clubs galore.

Channeling the cinematic stylings of French New Wave, cross-pollinated with the rebellious vibe of 90s-era Gregg Araki, F-Toys is rude, crude, unhinged, girlypop middle finger to filmic convention. It’s a surrealist and satirical odyssey with a cast to match that includes 13 Reasons Why’s Brandon Flynn, The Comeback’s Damian Young, and a knockout performance by Heated Rivarly’s François Arnaud. Sriram’s F-Toys took home a Special Jury Award at both SXSW & Fantasia, a Grand Jury Award at NewFest, and earned the writer-director a 2026 Film Independent Spirit Award Nomination.

events.title: Jaguar w/ Coffintexts
events.description:
Jaguar // feat. COFFINTEXTS & EPO (10/2)

Part Miami Bass, vintage house bounce, and tribal euphoria, Coffintexts’ music is a cocktail of indulgence
served straight from the queer underground.
When Coffintexts first burst onto the club scene in the late ‘10s, she was part of a new cohort of Miami
producers reshaping dance music. Equally influenced by everything from 90s tribal rhythms to Latin
American-inflected Club to UK rave, she emerged as part of the city’s new guard. Putting out records on
labels including Omnidisc, Club Romantico, Club QU, Classico, and a forthcoming record on TraTraTrax,
she has quickly established herself as one of the Magic City’s most vibrant musicians.

Even within this crowded field, Coffintexts acts as a unique center of gravity. While drawing from the
percussive promiscuity of her Peruvian heritage and the bass weight of her hometown, she also
gravitated towards the cerebral funk of ‘90s hardgroove, wiggly house, and the chromatic polish of UK
techno. Cutting her teeth in house parties and gay clubs across Miami, she’s always gravitated towards
the minimal, groove-focused energy of dance music at its most muscular and hypnotic. This background
has put her into conversation not just with the 305, but with the larger global queer dance music
cosmology.

There aren’t many producers and DJs who marry the paranoid and the psychedelic, the euphoric and the
illicit, the darkroom and the big room, the mind and the body, like Coffintexts.
As a producer, she’s just as comfortable turning out lean and stripped back techno as she is sultry,
bottom-heavy downtempo with occasional partner-in-crime Jonny from Space. Her DJing is just as
adventurous. Her mixes for outlets like Crack and Mixmag showcase an ambitious and daring style where
she jumps between tempos, eras, and genres without ever losing sight of that central current of hip-
swinging groove. It’s this intuitive and bodily approach to mixing that has kept dance floors from Miami to
Shanghai to Bristol, from Nowadays to III Points Festival to Razzmatazz gyrating and sweating it out until
the early hours.

Our dear friend EPO is back from Italy to get the crowd moving.

events.title: Birding Expedition: Powdermill Avian Research Center
events.venue_name: Powdermill Nature Reserve and Avian Research Center
events.description: Meet at Powdermill Nature Reserve and Avian Research CenterA photo-worthy day full of important conservation work, stunning views, and beautiful birds! Begin your day at the Powdermill Avian Research Center (PARC), part of the Carnegie Museum of Natural History’s Powdermill Nature Reserve. Here, you can watch skilled ornithologists gently capture, band, and release wild birds—an up-close look at avian research and conservation in action. It’s a rare chance to see warblers, thrushes, and other songbirds just inches away while learning about migration and habitat studies. Join the Aviary to zoom in on birds like warblers, thrushes, vireos, and flycatchers with Ornithologist Bob Mulvihill and Educator and Photographer Mike Faix, who will be able to provide interesting information and birding tales appealing to kids and adults alike. Bring your own binoculars, or borrow an Aviary pair that we'll help you use! Afterward, we continue our adventure into the Laurel Highlands with a visit to the Spruce Flats Bog, a unique high-elevation wetland surrounded by spruce and tamarack trees. A short boardwalk trail leads you through mossy hummocks and quiet pools where we may spot migrant birds on their journey south. Birding for Beginners is open to participants 6 years and older. Those under 16 must be accompanied by a registered adult. Binoculars will be available to borrow.

events.description: Elevate your basketry skills in this 4-part series and create an impressive, functional work of art! Basketry: Cherokee-Style Twill Floor Basket with Traycee Bosle four-part series Date: Saturdays October 3, 10, 17, 24 Time: 10AM-1 PM Description: Designed for students with some basketweaving experience, this four-week workshop explores the art of twill basketry through the creation of a striking floor basket in an elegant urn shape. Over four three-hour sessions, participants will learn the fundamentals of twill construction, including how to build a twill base, execute a dramatic double-diamond twill pattern, and shape the basket into a graceful urn form. Emphasis will be placed on technique, structure, and pattern development. Students will leave with an impressive, functional basket—perfect to enjoy at home or present as a memorable handmade gift. Tuition: $210 + $40 materials fee Note: Full and partial tuition scholarships are often available—with some limitations—to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Find more information and the scholarship application here. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Senior Education Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Materials: All materials will be provided. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Paper Studio, which is on the first floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Paper Studio from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 8 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. The Paper Studio is located down the hall from this entrance. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything that would be helpful for us to know before you arrive, please leave a message for Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or by email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Traycee Bosle is a professional basket weaver at Craftisinal Creative Works—her arts studio in Pittsburgh, PA. She is a member of the Handweavers Guild of America and the Fiber Arts Guild of Pittsburgh. With over 1500 works in several different weaving styles under her belt, you can find her work in homes across the U.S. Basketweaving is an ancient art that crosses nearly all time, geographic, political, and social boundaries. It’s rooted in history, mathematics and pattern, color theory and design—with so much to offer—yet it’s nearly a lost art. Traycee has made it her mission to share her love for this once ubiquitous and critical skill with people of all ages. Her classes are fun, informative and personalized! She provides hands-on, individualized instruction using her own specially designed basket kits to teach the fundamentals of the art and meet each student where they are in their skill level. Whether you are an absolute beginner or have already made a few baskets, you will walk away with new skills and a beautiful basket you can use every day.

events.title: Introduction to Woodturning: Pens with Matt Iannacci
events.description: Learn the basics of woodturning by making your own wooden ballpoint pen! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, October 3rd, 2026 Time: 10am–1pm Description: In this beginning woodturning workshop, students will learn the foundations of woodturning to turn their own wooden pen! This class will explore the lathe, different methods of shaping wood on it, and shop safety. All materials, including the pen hardware, are provided. This is a great project to begin your woodturning journey! Each student will leave with their own wooden ballpoint pen—handmade on the lathe by them! Special thanks to Turners Anonymous for the use of lathes during this workshop! Tuition: $80 + $20 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided. You will be working in a fully operational woodshop and we will go over all equipment safety precautions. Please arrive wearing closed toed shoes, no loose or baggy clothing, and long hair tied back. Location: Contemporary Craft Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist “I have been woodturning for over 10 years, and doing wood flatwork for more than 7 years. I focus on medium-sized peices (vases, urns, etc., in woodturning, and jewelry boxes and frames in flatwork), usually seeking to combine different wood species to provide color and texture in my pieces. I am also the inventor of the JS3 jig, which is used to set up for compound-angle cuts necessary for splayed-stave woodturning, or boxes with leaning walls.” Outside of woodworking, Matt is a full-time mechanical engineer, a dad, and a saxophone and flute-player in a jazz band in the North Hills in Pittsburgh.

events.title: Explore Allegheny West:  Riches, Writers & Reuse
events.address: Brighton Road and Western Avenue, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania 15212
events.description: Saturday, October 3, 2026$25.00 per personIn the 1890's, so many wealthy industrialists and merchants, built mansions in a section of what was then Allegheny City that one of the streets there was nicknamed Millionaire's Row. Men with the familiar last names of Jones, Laughlin, Phipps, and Kaufmann hired well-known architects to build their mansions and churches. A variety of Victorian architectural styles--Colonial Revival, Richardsonian Romanesque, Italianate, Second Empire, and Greek Revival--filled the streets. Many of the structures still stand in the area that is the destination of this tour: Allegheny West. Stroll along with our docents through Pittsburgh's smallest neighborhood as they talk about the area's affluent past, its prosperous present, and the buildings' architectural details. Highlights will include the house where America's Agatha Christie began her career, the birthplace of a famous ex-pat writer, and the home where the Steelers' Art & Dan Rooney lived. You also will learn how residents banded together in the 1960s to prevent urban renewal from altering their neighborhood's ambience. The tour also includes a brief excursion into the Allegheny Second Ward Industrial Historic District, which touches the northern-most border of Allegheny West and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2025.

events.title: Ki Ki B. Jones’ Charm School and Man Camp in the Steel City
events.description: Free one-day program will provide workshops addressing life skills, personal development and challenges facing today’s youthCharm School and Man Camp in the Steel City will return on Saturday, October 3, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at Faros Allegheny Center on Pittsburgh’s North Side.Sponsored by S&T Bank, the free program welcomes youth ages 10–17, with Charm School designed for girls and Man Camp designed for boys. Parents and guardians are also encouraged to attend and participate.Local professionals and community leaders will facilitate interactive workshops covering law and order, financial literacy, mental health, health and fitness, etiquette and entrepreneurship. The program will also address self-image and help young people navigate the pressures of social media, online bullying and the expectations they face every day.Charm School and Man Camp in the Steel City was created to equip young people with practical resources, positive role models and a safe environment where they can ask questions, build confidence and prepare for their futures. The program also encourages stronger communication between parents and children. Resource vendors will also be on hand to provide youth and parents will information and materials for educational programming, apprenticeships, counseling, and more Through honest conversations, engaging workshops and access to trusted community resources, Charm School and Man Camp in the Steel City aims to remind every participant that they are seen, valued and capable of achieving success.

events.title: History Alive! Meet the Sheep!
events.description: Come meet Jacky and Patsy and learn about the animals who lived at the Fort in the 18th century!We are so proud of our resident female ewes Jacky and Patsy, look how they are walking like little ladies.Why are they living at the Fort this fall? They are a distinctive feature of our History Alive! program. Animals were a vital part of the Forbes Campaign and Fort Ligonier’s history. From 1758 to 1766, thousands of horses, cattle, pigs, goats, and sheep helped feed the soldiers and transport the artillery and wagons. Most animals grazed outside the Fort with grass guards stationed close by.History Alive!, is an engaging experience for visitors to learn about the daily life of a frontier military outpost in North America during the 18th century. Weekends feature 18th-century-inspired artisans, tradesmen, musicians, historical interpreters, and more who depict the culture and lifestyle of the colonial era.History Alive! is generously funded by Americana Corner Preserving America Partners Grant Program.History Alive! programs are included with regular admission fees and are always free to Fort Ligonier Association members.

events.title: 16th Annual Ellwood City Oktoberfest
events.description: The 16th Annual Ellwood City Oktoberfest will be held Saturday, Oct 3, 2026 in Ewing Park, Ellwood City from 12pm to 5pm (Rain or Shine). This is a joint fundraiser for The Ellwood City Wolves Club, Den II and The Rotary Club of Ellwood City. Combined, the clubs have over 180 years of community service to the Ellwood City and surrounding area. The 16th Annual Ellwood City Oktoberfest highlights craft brewers, sampling of a variety of craft beers, raffles, auctions and games. The Wrangler Band will be on hand to provide music in the park. Food sampling includes: pretzels, pepperoni puffs, hulaski, beer cheese, saurkraut & kielbasi, a variety of sliders (pulled pork, fish,sausage and meatball), hotdogs and french fries.Check out all the great merchandise that has been generously donated that will be up for silent auction. There will be over 100 Buckets in the annual Bucket Raffle. Buckets include beers, beer merchandise and the metal bucket for cooling your beverages.Advanced Ticket are $35 or $40 at the door. The can be purchased through any member of the Wolves or Rotary Clubs, at Pete’s Uptown and Ellwood City Candy Company. Annually the Oktoberfest Committee designates a portion of the advanced ticket sales to go to a local organziation. This year proceeds will go to the Ellwood City Historical Society. It is through events such as the Oktoberfest that enables our clubs to provide over $20,000 annually in Academic and Trade School Scholarships for graduating students in the Ellwood and Riverside School Districts. It also goes to support community events like, Proms, Parades, Easter Egg Hunts as well as the local organizations such as the Food Bank, Club Hope, Carpenter’s Project, Fire Department, and the Local Library, to name a few.

events.title: Introduction to Weaving: Beginner Basics with Luca Budofsky
events.description: Weaving-curious? This workshop will introduce you to various types of looms, and will get you started weaving on a frame loom! Introduction to Weaving: Beginner Basics with Jamie Boyle 3-hour workshop Date: Saturday, October 3 Time: 2:00pm – 5:00pm Description: Curious about different kinds of looms? Want to try weaving but you are not sure where to start? Let this workshop be a beginning for you! Jamie will share some weaving basics and will guide you through weaving on a frame loom, which you will get to take home with you! Additionally, you will get to experience how some different types of looms function, including a rigid heddle loom and a multi-harness loom, guided by the general question: what does a loom do? In this class you will primarily work with your hands on a non-mechanical frame loom, but you will get an overview of various modes of weaving and get to try other looms in the studio! Tuition: $65 + $15 materials fee (if you are viewing this listing on your phone, scroll down to the bottom of the page for the class registration link) Materials: all materials are included. Registration: Register through Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available—with some limitations—to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Scholarship application is found at this link . You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, TImmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the Fibers Loft on the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. About the Artist Luca Budofsky is a multimedia artist from northern New Jersey. They hold a BFA from Carnegie Mellon University School of Art with a minor in Soft Technologies. They take particular interest in how textiles occupy shifting scales of material production and the way the woven structure breaks a surface into modular interlocking pieces. They love chance encounters with light casted on walls and sidewalks. They like noise. They think public radio is cool. They attribute their interest in cyclical events and repetitive processes to being a triplet. Luca has been recognized as an Andrew Carnegie Society Scholar and as a recipient of the Samuel Rosenberg Art Award. They work and weave in Pittsburgh, PA.
