events.title: Night of Death & Disaster
events.description:
Join us for our annual Halloween celebration, a Night of Death and Disaster! Come dressed in your best macabre couture as we dive deep into Warhol’s darker side for a night of eerie revelry, but help us protect our collection. No masks, wings, tails or other props that could bump the artwork.

-DJ set by Second Skin (Erica Scary & Huck Finn)
-Tarot readings by Three3Three and Pgh Astrology
-Take home your own spooky poems typed on a typewriter live by Sprouts of Consciousness
-Floral arrangements and decor by greenSinner
-Stay tuned: More mayhem to be announced!
-Please note: This event is for ages 21+.

This celebration sold out last year. Don’t miss out.

In his "Death and Disaster" series, Warhol explored the impact of images taken out of a journalistic context and framed, through repetition, as works of art. Some of the photographs that Warhol chose as source images for this series depict horrific scenes. Others focus on a narrative that may not be obvious, but is symbolic of death and disaster nonetheless, such as the Electric Chair and Jackie series. In all of these works, Warhol repeated images to mirror the repetition evident in society through media and technology.

Night of Death and Disaster is sponsored by Design Within Reach.

events.title: Drawing & Mark Making on Enamel with Andrew Thornton
events.description: Learn to embellish your enameled surfaces with drawing & mark making techniques! 7-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, October 24th Time: 10am-5pm Description: Enameling is a method of bonding glass to metal. It is a wonderful way to add color and vibrancy to your creations. In this class, we’ll be going one step further and exploring mark making and drawing on enameled surfaces. We will cover the different ways to prepare the drawing surfaces, go over what products will work to create your illustrations (and which ones won’t), and discuss finishing touches. This is great for 2D artists looking to put their artwork on jewelry or anyone looking to make their enameled pieces stand out. Not confident in drawing? That’s okay! Andrew will show step-by-step embellishment techniques that will convince others that you’re a capable illustrator. Tuition: $105 + $30 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided Location: Contemporary Craft – Raphael Building, Metals Studio (5645 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. If you require accessibility accommodations, please let us know by calling 412.261.7003 and we are happy to assist you. About the Artist Andrew Thornton is a professional fine artist, trained at the School of Visual Arts in New York City. He is a mixed media artist who works in painting, collage, metalsmithing, sculpture, polymer clay, resin, and jewelry. His work explores identity through magical realism and fantasy. He has projects that were featured in Kristal Wick’s book, “Foxy Epoxy” and was invited as a guest on the PBS shows, “Beads, Baubles, and Jewels” and “Make It Artsy”. Andrew is the Co-Owner and Creative Director of Allegory Gallery in Ligonier, PA. Allegory Gallery was one of SCORE’s 2018 American Small Business Championship winners. When he’s not creating art, making jewelry, or writing, he is working on Star Cottage Studio. Star Cottage Studio is a working studio in a 100 year old former school house. Andrew recently was appointed as a Board Member for Touchstone Center for Crafts and was awarded one of the Artist-in- Residence positions in the Metal Studio at Contemporary Craft in Pittsburgh, PA. He and his partner, William, live in their happy home with three cats, artwork covering every wall, and lots and lots of books and beads!

events.title: SPECIAL TOUR: HISTORIC THORNBURG, PA
events.description: Saturday, October 24, 202610:00 am to 12:00 pm$25.00 per personRising on a bluff above the valley carved by the Chartiers Creek, the Borough of Thornburg is a little piece of Southern California in southwestern Pennsylvania. The planned suburb was created in 1899 by Frank Thornburg and his cousin David on land that had been in the family since 1806. Early houses built here were in the Queen Anne Style. By 1904, however, the Pittsburgh Gazette celebrated the "model and aristocratic suburb" for its "most unique collection of houses near Pittsburgh." The variety of historical residential styles would soon be augmented by homes inspired by Frank Thornburg's personal passion: the contemporary Mission-and Craftsman-style houses he saw and studied during travels in Los Angeles and vicinity. With a willing accomplice in his cousin, architect Samuel McClarren, Thornburg would create an enclave that still retains its architectural and natural integrity and that continues to delight with its tough of SoCal style.

events.title: Beginner Woodworking: Steelers Flight Board with John Henley
events.description: Celebrate the return of Fall Football Season by making a custom Pittsburgh-themed flight board! (just in time for the France Game!) 4-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Time: 11am–3pm Description: Make your Pittsburgh-themed flight board! Students will explore the foundations of woodworking – from milling a slab into a project board, to dowel joints, to finishing a fun custom project. First, we’ll mill a rough-sawn board into surfaced lumber. Then, we’ll add dowel feet and drill holes for drinking glass. Finally, students will choose from a variety of Pittsburgh-themed engraved coasters to inlay into their boards, from our sports teams to Jalapeno Hannah to an Eat’n’Park cookie – only Pittsburgh icons! Come with no woodworking experience and leave with a handmade souvenir celbrating your favorite sports team! Tuition: $90 + $25 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided. Location: Contemporary Craft Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. If you require accessibility accommodations, please let us know by calling 412.261.7003 and we are happy to assist you. About the Artist John Henley is a woodworker, designer, and researcher who creates functional objects that build connection with the materials, landscapes, and people surrounding us. John received a B.Des in Industrial Design from Carnegie Mellon University and served as an apprentice for master woodworker Tadao Arimoto. Having grown up in Oregon and now based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, John’s interest in the landscape—both natural and built—impacts his work, which combines traditional craft practices and contemporary praxis. John has received multiple awards and residencies, including a fellowship with the Steve Jobs Archive and, currently, an apprenticeship with Contemporary Craft, where he is supporting arts education while maintaining a studio practice.

Gonzalez, directed by Shaunda Miles McDill, and starring Cynthia Dallas and Michael Patrick Trimm, this high-stakes modern reimagining brings Shakespeare to the Northside stage. When Imani Othello is named Head Coach of America's most beloved football franchise, the pressure mounts on and off the field. This hard-hitting adaptation centers a Black woman calling the plays at the height of her power, confronting ambition, betrayal, and relentless doubt.

•	Tickets: $50 (Thursday, Oct. 22: Pay-What-You-Can starting at $20)

events.title: Mike Super - Magic and Illusion
events.description: Mike Super – Magic and Illusion: Mike Super is an award-winning illusionist and entertainer renowned for blending astonishing magic with humor, audience participation, and captivating storytelling. Rising to national prominence through his appearances on television talent competitions and magic specials, he has earned a reputation for creating performances that combine grand illusions with intimate moments that leave audiences questioning what they just witnessed. Rather than relying solely on visual spectacle, Super's shows emphasize personal connection, weaving comedy, suspense, and interactive demonstrations into an experience that appeals to families and magic enthusiasts alike. Fans attending a Mike Super performance can expect an unforgettable evening filled with mind-bending illusions, impossible feats, and engaging moments that transform spectators into active participants in the magic.

events.title: Noel Paul Stookey
events.venue_name: Carnegie Music Hall of Oakland - Pittsburgh
events.description: Noel Paul Stookey is an acclaimed singer-songwriter best known as the “Paul” of the legendary folk trio Peter, Paul and Mary. His solo performances draw on a remarkable catalog that includes “The Wedding Song (There Is Love),” alongside folk, jazz, spiritual, and socially conscious music. Stookey describes his distinctive blend of folk lyrics and jazz improvisation as “fazz,” a style showcased throughout his solo work. A longtime advocate for social change, he continues to connect music with messages of justice, inclusion, hope, and community action.

events.title: SkyWatch: Life on Moons
events.description: Is there anyone out there? Uncover how NASA has looked for key elements of life on moons in our solar systems and how the Cassini mission contributed to these efforts. Draw an extreme environment beyond Earth and invent a living thing that could survive there, modeling NASA scientists’ study on extremophiles. Build a spacecraft and put it through a series of tests to ensure it’s ready to launch. Additionally, enjoy a planetarium show and stargazing time on the observatory deck (weather-permitting). Viewing targets include Saturn, the Moon, and Pleiades, an open star cluster located about 440 light-years away in the constellation Taurus.

events.title: 2 SQUARE IMPROV
events.description: We couldnt be more excited to welcome 2 Square to the bottlerocket stage especially after seeing their amazing set this year ar UCB's DCM 26'. Two of the best John Lutz and Peter Grosz take a single suggestion then spin that into a longform show featuring a kaleidoscope of scenes, absurdist transitional elements and callbacks – all while never once using a “sweep edit” to get from scene to scene. John Lutz has been acting, improvising and writing for over 30 years. You may know him best as Lutz from 30 Rock. Other screen appearances include: Loot, Girls5Eva, Chicago Med, The Good Wife and Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt. Film credits include The Comedian, Sisters and Sleepwalk with Me. He wrote for Saturday Night Live from 2004-2010 and is currently in his 12th year writing for Late Night with Seth Meyers. For 3 years, he toured the world from Bangkok to Rockford, IL with The Second City National Touring Company. He recently wrote the NY Times bestselling audiobook Escape from Virtual Island. He created, co-wrote and produced the series Mapleworth Murders with Paula Pell,which is streaming on Roku. Peter Grosz has been teaching improvisation and writing at various theaters across America for the last 25 years. He wrote and performed in four reviews with The Second City ETC and was a founding member of the experimental improv groups JTS Brown, 4 Square and 2 Square. He has written for The Colbert Report, Late Night With Seth Meyers and At Home With Amy Sedaris, winning two Emmys, three WGA awards and a Peabody along the way. You’ve seen him in The Menu, Veep, The Bear, The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel, The President Show and more. You can hear him on Wait Wait, Don’t Tell Me on NPR and he was in a few commercials for Sonic drive-in, but only for 18 years so you might have missed them. Seating/Show Information: This show will have theater seating. Seats will be assigned upon arrival, or can be chosen ahead of time for an additional fee. QR Code Ordering will be available for this performance. Doors open at 9pm. Don't miss our famous Bottlerocket Pre-Show Clip Collection, beginning one hour before the start of the performance. This show is ALL AGES *all information subject to change as needed. Bottlerocket FAQ: All shows starting before 10pm are all ages unless otherwise noted. Free parking is available at 824 Industry Street and 205 Allen Street, as well as other public lots in the area. Live Music shows have limited seating options, please arrive early or reach out to the venue directly if you know that you require a seat. Doors open at 5pm for all shows unless noted otherwise. The time listed on the ticket is the event's true start time. Most shows have a preshow experience starting 1 hour before the show. Our full refund policy can be viewed here Please contact us ahead of time with any accesibilty requests or concerns, we're happy to accomodate you. More FAQ's can be found here

Step onto the 50-yard line for the New Hazlett’s first-ever co-production with DEMASKUS Theater Collective: Othello of the End Zone, or The Steel City Tragedy. Written by Franky D. Gonzalez, directed by Shaunda Miles McDill, and starring Cynthia Dallas and Michael Patrick Trimm, this high-stakes modern reimagining brings Shakespeare to the Northside stage. When Imani Othello is named Head Coach of America's most beloved football franchise, the pressure mounts on and off the field. This hard-hitting adaptation centers a Black woman calling the plays at the height of her power, confronting ambition, betrayal, and relentless doubt.
•	Dates: October 22–24 at 7:30 PM | October 24 at 2:00 PM | October 25 at 3:00 PM
•	Tickets: $50 (Thursday, Oct. 22: Pay-What-You-Can starting at $20)

events.title: The Lowest Pair
events.description: Doors 6PM | Show 7PM$15 ADV | $20 DOSThe Lowest PairThe Lowest Pair has questions. The duo, made up of Kendl Winter and Palmer T. Lee, know that we tend to see duality as a problem. We want life to be linear, working through the dark to finally get to the light. Grief to joy, despair to hope, confusion to claritynot a jangly cycle we cant escape. But through their incandescent folk songs, the Lowest Pair often ask: What if we sit with the mess? What if thats not just more peaceful, but more magical, too? Fare thee well and go to hell, I love you and Im mad at you. Its such a theme in my life, Winter says, then laughs. Wishing things were different but loving all of it, too.On their 8th album Always As Young As Well Ever Be, the Lowest Pair prove that over the last dozen years together, theyve become some of modern roots musics most mesmerizing, thoughtful purveyors. Produced by Tucker Martine (The Decemberists), the 10-track album puts the duos stark lyricism, string-driven arrangements, and raw compatibility on brilliant display. Were both trying to make space for each other rather than crowd each other out, Lee says, reflecting on why the Lowest Pair works. Were doing a lot of listening and reacting to what the other person is doing. Lees speaking voice is a comforting echo of his singing voice, soft and precise. Winter talks like she sings, too, sweet and raspy. Heard together, the effect is both soothing and scintillating, like a crisp mountain stream smoothing rocks. The Lowest Pairs musicianship is another beautiful testament not just to playing that breathes, but playing that listens. Winter, who grew up in Arkansas but has lived in Washington State for the last two decades, and Lee, a Minnesota native, first gained attention as poetic singer-songwriters on banjos. While their family of strings has expandedWinter plays more guitar on the new record than she ever has beforetheir fundamental approach hasnt: Respond to sounds and stories the other is making.

events.title: Creed Fisher
events.description: Creed Fisher is a West Texas singer-songwriter known for blending traditional country with modern elements and hard-rock influence. His music draws on working-class themes, patriotism and personal experience. Fisher’s notable releases include the albums Old School, which reached No. 3 on the iTunes Country Albums chart, and Hellraiser, which debuted at No. 2. His catalog also includes the songs “I’ll Keep Drinkin’,” “Ain’t Scared to Bleed” and “Fairies Wear Boots,” a cover of the Black Sabbath classic.

events.title: Prayers
events.description: Prayers is a San Diego-based electronic rock duo known for pioneering “cholo goth,” a distinctive fusion of darkwave, goth rock, synth-pop and Mexican-American street culture. Founded by Leafar Seyer and Dave Parley, the project pairs moody synthesizers, throbbing electronic rhythms and introspective vocals with a bold visual identity. Their catalog includes the albums *SD Killwave*, *Young Gods* and *Baptism of Thieves*, along with collaborations connected to Christian Death and other alternative artists. For listeners drawn to atmospheric, boundary-pushing rock and dark electronic music, Prayers offers an immersive performance rooted in self-expression and genre-defying creativity.

events.title: Phillip Phillips
events.description: Phillip Phillips is a platinum-selling singer-songwriter whose warm, soulful voice and blend of folk, rock, pop, and Americana have made him one of the most recognizable artists to emerge from American Idol. After winning the competition's eleventh season, he achieved immediate success with the multi-platinum hit "Home," followed by fan favorites including "Gone, Gone, Gone," "Raging Fire," and "Miles." Known for his heartfelt songwriting and acoustic-driven sound, Phillips draws inspiration from roots rock, blues, and contemporary singer-songwriter traditions, creating music that emphasizes authenticity, resilience, and human connection. His live performances showcase expressive vocals, accomplished guitar playing, and a relaxed stage presence that allows audiences to connect with both his chart-topping singles and deeper album cuts. Through years of touring and consistently evolving as a songwriter, Phillip Phillips has established himself as a respected artist whose timeless melodies and sincere storytelling continue to resonate with fans around the world.

events.title: Ten Evenings: Michael Lewis
events.description: An inside look at the early days of Trump’s Department of Government Efficiency, as told by the public servants it targeted and one of America’s best storytellers.Blockers. It wasn’t a compliment. In the new Washington, it was the worst thing you could be—especially if you worked in the federal government and wanted to keep your job. A Blocker was a holdover, an impediment, someone who didn’t get the message—and, most of all, someone who didn’t belong.Michael Lewis found seven of them.Blockers is the story of people who believed they had a calling, who were convinced they were doing something the country couldn’t do without, and then discovered they were no longer wanted. One kept Americans’ most sensitive tax data out of the wrong hands and another made sure that politicians and civil servants played by the rules. One figured out how to stop wildfires from destroying suburban neighborhoods, another helped uncover the mysteries of cystic fibrosis.There was also a security guard.It should come as no surprise that the writer who made subprime mortgages gripping (The Big Short) and who turned baseball statistics into poetry (Moneyball) could transform the first two years of the second Trump administration into a thriller about federal employees. But he does.And he does something else. He puts before us a clear question: If these public servants can’t survive in government today, then what does that say about us?New York Times bestselling author Michael Lewis has published many books on subjects ranging from politics to Wall Street. Lewis’s most recent #1 New York Times bestselling book, Going Infinite, tells the story of FTX’s collapse and the enigmatic founder at its center, Sam Bankman-Fried.Lewis is the creator and host of Apple’s #1 rated podcast Against the Rules, a searing look at what’s happened to fairness in American life through the lens of people who depend on public trust.Mr. Lewis grew up in New Orleans and remains deeply interested and involved in the city. He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Art History from Princeton and a Master’s degree in Economics from the London School of Economics. He lives in Berkeley, California, with his wife, Tabitha Soren, and their children.

events.title: Hadestown - The Musical - Pittsburgh, PA
events.description: COME SEE HOW THE WORLD COULD BE. Welcome to HADESTOWN, where a song can change your fate. Winner of eight 2019 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy® Award for Best Musical Theater Album, this acclaimed new show from celebrated singer-songwriter Anaïs Mitchell and original director Rachel Chavkin (Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812) is a love story for today... and always. HADESTOWN intertwines two mythic tales — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone — as it invites you on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Mitchell’s beguiling melodies and Chavkin’s poetic imagination pit industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love. Performed by a vibrant ensemble of actors, dancers and singers, HADESTOWN is a haunting and hopeful theatrical experience that grabs you and never lets go.

events.title: Sleeping with Sirens w/ Rain City Drive
events.description: Sleeping With Sirens is a post-hardcore band that has become one of the defining acts of its generation through a combination of emotional songwriting, soaring melodies, and energetic live performances. Fronted by vocalist Kellin Quinn, whose distinctive high-register voice has become instantly recognizable within the rock community, the band rose to prominence with albums such as With Ears to See and Eyes to Hear, Let's Cheers to This, and Feel. Their music frequently explores themes of perseverance, relationships, self-discovery, and personal resilience, helping them connect deeply with fans around the world. Joining the tour, Rain City Drive brings a modern rock sound built on powerful vocals, polished production, and a blend of alternative, post-hardcore, and hard rock influences that have earned the band a rapidly growing audience. Also appearing on the bill is SHYEYE, an emerging artist known for combining emotionally driven songwriting with contemporary rock elements, adding a fresh perspective to a lineup that showcases both established favorites and rising talent. Together, these performers create a diverse concert experience that highlights the continued evolution of modern rock while delivering the passion and intensity that fans have come to expect from the genre.

events.description: Hadestown is a Tony Award-winning musical that reimagines the ancient Greek myths of Orpheus and Eurydice through a modern blend of folk, jazz, blues, and theatrical storytelling. Set in a hauntingly atmospheric world, the production explores themes of love, sacrifice, hope, and the struggle between freedom and control. The show is celebrated for its emotionally powerful music, poetic lyrics, and visually striking stage design that creates an immersive theatrical experience. With its inventive retelling of classic mythology and unforgettable score, Hadestown has become one of the most acclaimed contemporary musicals on Broadway and tour.

events.title: Spirits of Hallowe'en History Tours
events.description: Step into the shadows this Hallowe'en at West Overton Village & Museum! Explore the eerie origins of Halloween traditions from ancient Celtic rituals to Victorian parties and today's trick or treat. Uncover the dark and fascinating history behind your favorite haunted holiday. Local Halloween celebrations once spanned days of frightful fun. Learn about the debauchery of Chalk Night and Mischief Night across southwestern Pennsylvania. Hear true tales of neighborhood pranks from the ever-popular “corning” to more dangerous hijinks: wheelbarrows hanging from telephone poles, signs missing from buildings, and entire wagons hoisted onto roofs. Tour the 1838 Overholt Homestead by candlelight. Try some Victorian fortune telling party games: Who will be your future love? Will you become wealthy? Who in your group will meet an untimely demise?Stop by a re-created 1800s Halloween party and enjoy a variety of historical treats. Written using dozens of local newspaper articles and historical sources, this immersive tour delves into the real history of Hallow’s Eve.Plan your visitTours are available at 6:00, 6:30, 7:00, and 7:30 on October 28, 29, and 30.Each tour is approximately one hour and involves walking outdoors, up and down stairs, and in the dark. Please register in advance - tours have limited capacity and we cannot guarantee there will be tickets available at the door.

events.title: Barbara Kingsolver in conversation with Anna Singer
events.description: The story of a brief, passionate, life-changing love affair, wrapped up in what might be the greatest romance of all: our eternal human longing for art and beauty.Livia Cable has made her peace with her marriage and modest livelihood in the farm country where she grew up, until a shocking phone call from an old lover shakes her to the core. Decades earlier, this man knew her as Livia Bohusz, a music conservatory student estranged from her home and family, uncertain of anything except her passion for music and promise as an extraordinary pianist. His request, now, to see her again stirs up ghosts she’s kept at bay for a lifetime.Shifting between past and present, Livia’s decision to meet or reject the reunion means confronting step by step, in memories framed as musical dances, the experiences of childhood loss, abandonment, self-immolating passion, and perilous attachment to a man who broke her belief in love and ruptured the course of her life.With razor-sharp acuity and deep affection, Pulitzer Prize winner Barbara Kingsolver’s unforgettable new novel reflects on class barriers, the risks of ambition, and the timeless, life-changing power of art.Barbara Kingsolver is the author of ten bestselling works of fiction, including the novels Unsheltered, The Bean Trees, and The Poisonwood Bible, as well as books of poetry, essays, creative nonfiction, and Coyote’s Wild Home, a children’s book co-authored with Lily Kingsolver. She also collaborated with family members on the influential Animal, Vegetable, Miracle: A Year of Food Life. Kingsolver’s work has been translated into more than thirty languages and has earned a devoted readership at home and abroad. She is a member of the American Academy of Arts and Letters, and has received numerous awards and honors including the 2023 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for her novel, Demon Copperhead, the National Humanities Medal, and most recently, the National Book Foundation’s Medal for Distinguished Contribution to American Letters. She lives with her husband on a farm in southern Appalachia.

events.description: We are embracing Hannibal and horror for “The Silence of the Lambs Cage Night” as our historic building is transformed into two full floors of seasonal entertainment and spooky thrills. The heart of this event is a life-sized replica of Hannibal’s cage, complete with a live Hannibal Lecter and the original rug and bed-frame from the film. Who will be brave enough to get a photo with Hannibal, in the same room where the infamous cage scene was filmed…?! Speaking of scary, costumes are encouraged. However, please no full-face masks or weapons. Stroll the vendor marketplace, featuring some of the spookiest merchandise and entertainment in Pittsburgh. A variety of specialty refreshments will be available to purchase, including a cash bar for guests ages 21 and older. If you do intend to partake, please be sure to bring a valid photo ID.

events.description: Grateful Shred is a collective of accomplished musicians dedicated to celebrating the music and improvisational spirit of the Grateful Dead through vibrant, guitar-driven performances. Known for their exceptional musicianship and deep appreciation of the Dead’s catalog, the group delivers faithful interpretations while embracing the spontaneity and exploration that define jam-band culture. Their concerts feature intricate harmonies, extended instrumental passages, and a relaxed yet energetic atmosphere that appeals to both longtime Deadheads and newer audiences. By combining technical skill with a genuine love for the music, Grateful Shred creates an engaging live experience that honors the enduring legacy of the Grateful Dead.

events.title: THE OLD ALLEGHENY COUNTY JAIL AND MUSEUM-FREE
events.description: Open on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of the month except on Court holidays.Visit at your convenience between 11:30 am and 1:00 pm--Cost: FREEPHLF docents are on hand to tell you the story of the former Allegheny County Jail. Completed in 1886 to the designs of Boston architect H.H. Richardson, it closed on July 27, 1995. The building was then renovated between 1995 and 2001 and adapted for a new use as the Family Division of the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas. Working with the leadership of Allegheny County and with funding from the Drue Heinz Trust, our organization coordinated with the former jail's Deputy Warden Ed Urban and the Allegheny County Juvenile Court to preserve one portion of the cell blocks of the historic jail to create the Old Allegheny County Jail Museum. The Jail Museum, located in Downtown--at 440 Ross Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15219--opened in 2005.To access the Museum: Enter the Family Court Building through the main entrance on Ross Street. You will then be processed through a security checkpoint. The Museum is located across from the vending machine room. The use of cameras is NOT permitted.

events.title: Turning Night! Guided Open Studio with Matt Iannacci
events.description: Open to anyone who's tried their hand at woodturning, come spend the evening making your latest project under Matt's guidance! 3-Hour Guided Open Studio Date: Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Time: 6–9pm Description: Spend the evening on the lathes with fellow turners! Join us for Turning Night, a guided open studio session open to anyone who’s taken a woodturning workshop with us before—or anyone with experience on a wood lathe at all! Come with a project idea and Matt will guide you through the setup and technique to make it happen. This is the perfect opportunity for anyone with some turning experience to pursue their own project—but in the presence of an experienced woodturning instructor! The Studio has a small selection of turning blanks for sale, including pen blanks ( pen kit available here ), spindle blanks, and bowl blanks. However, for a more specific project, students are welcome to bring a wood blank of their own (we recommend Rockler if purchasing in advance). Join us for a night of woodturning community, guidance, and fun! Thanks to Turners Anonymous for the use of lathes during this workshop and Matt Iannacci for his expertise and enthusiasm! Tuition: $45 Materials: The Studio has a small selection of turning blanks for sale, or students can BYOB (blank)! Location: Contemporary Craft Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. If you require accessibility accommodations, please let us know by calling 412.261.7003 and we are happy to assist you. About the Artist: Matt Iannacci “I have been woodturning for over 10 years, and doing wood flatwork for more than 7 years. I focus on medium-sized peices (vases, urns, etc., in woodturning, and jewelry boxes and frames in flatwork), usually seeking to combine different wood species to provide color and texture in my pieces. I am also the inventor of the JS3 jig, which is used to set up for compound-angle cuts necessary for splayed-stave woodturning, or boxes with leaning walls.” Outside of woodworking, Matt is a full-time mechanical engineer, a dad, and a saxophone and flute-player in a jazz band in the North Hills in Pittsburgh.

events.title: Judy Collins
events.description: Judy Collins is a legendary folk singer-songwriter known for her crystal-clear vocals, poetic songwriting, and influential role in the American folk music revival of the 1960s. Her music blends folk, pop, and traditional ballad influences while often exploring themes of love, social awareness, introspection, and human connection. Collins became widely respected for interpreting songs by iconic songwriters and for helping introduce audiences to many influential artists throughout her long career. With decades of acclaimed performances, timeless recordings, and a graceful stage presence, Judy Collins remains one of the most celebrated voices in folk and contemporary acoustic music.

events.title: Needle Felting: Bird of the Month: Chickadee with Erin Carlson
events.description: November’s bird of the month: Chickadee! Learn to needle felt, while enjoying a detailed look at this fascinating bird! 3-hour workshop Date: Thursday, November 5 Time: 6pm-9pm Description: Learn to needle felt or sharpen your skills while creating your own Chickadee . Fiber artist and backyard bird enthusiast Erin Carlson of Red Cottage Fiber Studio will guide you through the needle felting process as you look closely to observe the shape and markings of the species and gain a deeper appreciation of our avian neighbors. Adventurous beginners welcome. Please note that we will be using sharp needles and repetitive, detailed hand motions. About the 2026-27 Bird of the Month Needle Felting Series : Due to popular demand, Contemporary Craft is thrilled to once again partner with instructor Erin Carlson to offer this series of workshops! While first offered virtually during the pandemic, this year will be live and in-person! Classes will occur the first Thursday of each month from 6-9pm and run from March 2026-February 2027. Join us for as many classes as you like. Choose your favorite bird or join us for all 12 to complete your very own flock. The bird selections are as follows: March: American Robin April: Scarlet Tanager May: Barn Swallow June: Eastern Bluebird July: Ruby-Throated Hummingbird August: American Goldfinch September: Downy Woodpecker October: Barn Owl November: Chickadee December: Northern Cardinal January(2027): Red Breasted Nuthatch February(2027): Red Winged Blackbird Tuition: $65 + $10 materials fee (per workshop) (if you are viewing this listing on your phone, scroll down to the bottom of the page for the class registration link) Materials: all materials are included. Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Scholarship application is found at this link . You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, TImmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the Fibers Loft on the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. About the Artist Erin Carlson is a multidiscplinary fiber artist working and teaching in th Pittsburgh area for the last decade. She loves to help students explore their creativity through the use of fibers.

events.title: Matilda - The Musical
events.description: Matilda – The Musical is a Tony Award-winning and Olivier Award-winning stage production that brings Roald Dahl's beloved story to life through imaginative storytelling, unforgettable songs, and spectacular choreography. Featuring a clever score by Tim Minchin and a book by Dennis Kelly, the musical follows the brilliant and determined young Matilda Wormwood as she discovers the power of courage, friendship, and imagination while standing up to injustice. Packed with witty humor, larger-than-life characters, and visually inventive staging, the production balances heartfelt emotion with high-energy musical numbers that appeal to audiences of all ages. From the unforgettable Miss Trunchbull to the kindhearted Miss Honey, each character contributes to a story that celebrates intelligence, resilience, and the belief that even the smallest voice can make a profound difference. With its award-winning music, inspiring message, and extraordinary theatrical creativity, Matilda – The Musical continues to delight theatergoers around the world as one of the most acclaimed family musicals of the modern era.

events.title: Andi Gladwin in Shuffled
events.description: Andi Gladwin's new intimate magic show unveils a mesmerizing fusion of storytelling, technology, and your very own deck of cards! An electrifying evening of magic awaits you for this brand-new show, developed exclusively for performances at Liberty Magic.Each guest is invited to bring their own deck of cards. A deck kept from Grandmother’s Bridge game? A tourist deck from your last vacation? The family Uno deck? Whatever the deck, bring it along, and it will become part of the show in the hands of a master of sleight-of-hand.British magician Andi Gladwin has dedicated his life to magic as co-founder of Vanishing Inc., one of the world’s largest magic brands, and as an in-demand performer. He has performed all over the world at prestigious events such as in Washington, DC for President Obama’s Inauguration, the world's most expensive private yacht, and more.“The best magic creates a story,” Andi says. “My aim is for everyone to walk away with a new experience that they will talk about for the rest of their lives.” Those stories have been told by guests at thousands of events over the past decade.Andi was a winner of Penn & Teller: Fool Us, where he managed to leave the magic duo completely dumfounded. He has also appeared on British ITV's Next Great Magician and is a season regular on CW Channel's Masters of Illusion. His magic is funny, upbeat, and downright deceiving. You’ll be talking about it for years to come, and you’ll never look at that family deck of cards in the same way again.“I can confidently say that ‘Shuffled’ is one of the best close-up magic shows I have ever witnessed.” — Suburban Chicagoland

events.title: Jesse Cook
events.description: Jesse Cook is an acclaimed Canadian guitarist, composer, and producer celebrated for his distinctive blend of nuevo flamenco, rumba, jazz, world music, and contemporary instrumental sounds. His performances showcase expressive nylon-string guitar work, intricate rhythms, and a richly atmospheric style shaped by musical influences from Spain, Latin America, the Middle East, and beyond. Cook’s extensive catalog includes fan favorites such as *Tempest*, *Gravity*, *The Rumba Foundation*, and *Beyond Borders*. His latest album, *past the breakwater*, is scheduled for release on September 18, 2026, offering a timely introduction to the evolving artistry of this internationally recognized musician.

events.title: Colby T. Helms
events.description: DOORS 7PM | SHOW 8PM$18 ADV | $23Every town has them. The underdogs. The people who never quite fit in. The ones who are misunderstood. The ones who strive, stumble, and keep going anyway.With his second album, One for the Losers, Colby T. Helms tells their stories.Raised in the Blue Ridge foothills of Southwest Virginia, Helms launched his career as a teenager, writing raw and ragged songs that drew from the people, places, stories, and struggles that shaped him. If his debut album chronicled his own experience, then One for the Losers widens the frame by looking outward. Across a dozen tracks, Helms shines a light on the overlooked and misunderstood characters whove crossed his path, from troubled friends and fallen mentors to moonshiners, immigrants, and working-class Virginians trying to survive in a world that threatens to leave them behind.

events.title: “Road to Revolution” Seminar at Fort Ligonier
events.description: Join us for an extraordinary two-day "Road to Revolution" Seminar featuring a distinguished panel of speakers who will discuss Revolutionary moments in history to celebrate America's 250th anniversary!For America’s Semiquincentenial anniversary, Fort Ligonier is partnering with Emerging Revolutionary War Era to bring you all the REVOLUTIONARY information you desire! Learn about the crucial ties that connect the French and Indian War to the War for American Independence with Revolutionary topics!2026 Seminar Speakers: Michael C. HarrisMichael C. Harris is a graduate of the University of Mary Washington and American Military University. He has worked with the National Park Service in Fredericksburg, Virginia; Fort Mott State Park in New Jersey; and the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission at Brandywine Battlefield. Mike has led tours and staff rides at numerous East Coast battlefields. His first book, Brandywine, received the American Revolution Round Table of Richmond Book Award in 2014.Daniel WelchDan Welch has served as editor of Gettysburg Magazine, a National Park Service ranger at Gettysburg National Military Park, and Education Programs Coordinator for the Gettysburg Foundation. He co-authored two books in the Emerging Civil War Series: The Last Road North: A Guide to the Gettysburg Campaign, 1863 and Never Such a Campaign: The Battle of Second Manassas, August 28–30, 1862. His latest work, Conquer or Die: The 1776 New York Campaign, explores the important but often overlooked battles for New York during the Revolution’s pivotal year.Greg Urwin, Ph.D.Gregory J.W. Urwin is a professor of history at Temple University, a prize-winning author, and a former president of the Society for Military History. He recently retired as general editor of the Campaigns and Commanders book series at University of Oklahoma Press, which he helmed since 1999. A specialist in U.S. and British military history, Urwin earned his PhD at the University of Notre Dame. During Professor Urwin’s decades of teaching, he trained twenty-six Ph.D.’s in military history.Urwin is an award-winning author whose work has been recognized by the Marine Corps Historical Foundation, the Little Big Horn Associates, and the Eastern National Park and Monument Association. He has written nine books, including his latest, When Freedom Wore a Red Coat: The British, the Enslaved, and the War in the South, 1780-81. He has also appeared in numerous documentaries, including programs on the History Channel and Pennsylvania Cable Network.Kevin J. Weddle, Ph.D.Kevin Weddle is a Distinguished Fellow and a military historian at the US Army War College in Carlisle, Pennsylvania. He is a graduate of the US Military Academy, a combat veteran, and served over 28 years on active duty in the US Army before retiring as a colonel. He is a multiple award-winning author of books and articles, including the critically acclaimed and best-selling The Compleat Victory: Saratoga and the American Revolution (Oxford University Press, 2021), winner of six national and international literary awards including the Gilder Lehrman Prize in Military History and the Society of the Cincinnati Prize. He leads military and civilian groups to battlefields around the world and specializes in the American Revolution, the American Civil War, the Second World War, general military history, and military technology.James M. Vaughn, Ph.D. “The Great War for Empire and the Origins of the American Revolution: A Revisionist Account.”James M. Vaughn is a historian of the global British Empire and the Atlantic world during the eighteenth century. He teaches at the University of Chicago, where he serves as an Associate Instructional Professor in the College and an Affiliate Faculty Member in the Department of History. He is the author of The Politics of Empire at the Accession of George III: The East India Company and the Crisis and Transformation of Britain’s Imperial State (Yale University Press), the co-editor of Envisioning Empire: The New British World from 1763 to 1773 (Bloomsbury) and Capitalism: Histories (Boydell & Brewer) and is currently writing a book on the origins of the American Revolution.About the “Road to Revolution” Seminar and the Braddock Road Preservation AssociationThe “Road to Revolution” Seminar honors the legacy of the Braddock Road Preservation Association.The Braddock Road Preservation Association was formed in 1989 as the Jumonville Preservation Association. It was formed to research, develop, interpret and promote the French and Indian War history of Jumonville, Dunbar’s Camp, and the Braddock Road. In 2025, the organization was dissolved after 36 years, but their seminar continues at Fort Ligonier.Fort Ligonier is partnering this year with the Emerging Revolutionary War (ERW) ERW, which serves as a public history-oriented platform dedicated to sharing original scholarship and discussion on the American Revolution. The ERW encourages our citizens to learn about our nation’s founding at the original places where the historic events occurred via their blog, podcasts, tours, and on-site videos.

events.title: Chat Pile
events.description: Chat Pile is an Oklahoma City noise-rock and sludge-metal band known for abrasive guitars, heavy rhythms, and stark examinations of social violence and decay. The group broke through with God’s Country (2022), a widely acclaimed debut that includes “Slaughterhouse” and “Why,” then expanded its sound on Cool World (2024). Chat Pile’s name references toxic mining-waste piles in northeastern Oklahoma, a fitting emblem for music that combines industrial weight, confrontational vocals, and bleak, sharply observed songwriting.

events.title: G. Clanton: Mainstream Now Tour
events.description:
George Clanton
w/ support from Ryan Hemsworth

⚡️ FRI NOVEMBER 6TH ⚡️
~spirit hall~

• tickets on sale tomorrow (8/7) @ 10AM •

George Clanton doesn’t just produce gleaming electronic pop, he produces nostalgia too. The Los Angeles artist’s process involves tweaking synthesizer presets, but beyond searching for the right melodies and textures, he’s hoping to come upon a sound that strikes a spiritual chord. “I’m looking for something that triggers a memory or an emotion,” he says. His lyrics are direct transmissions from his soul: raw, often off-the-cuff, evocative. When you pair those words with the gauzy textures Clanton’s become known for, his music feels like a dreamy filter you can put over your own memories. Every moment feels a little more colorful, a little more comforting.

events.description: WesGhost is an emerging alternative artist known for pairing moody production, melodic vocals, and emotionally direct songwriting into a sound that moves between pop, rock, hip-hop, and dark electronic influences. Through streaming platforms and social media, WesGhost has developed a growing audience drawn to his atmospheric soundscapes, vulnerable lyrics, and visually distinctive artistic identity. Tracks across his catalog showcase a talent for combining catchy hooks with shadowy textures, allowing him to stand out within the modern wave of genre-blending alternative performers. As his fan base continues to expand, WesGhost is establishing himself as a compelling new voice for listeners who gravitate toward emotional storytelling, late-night energy, and music that blurs the line between vulnerability and edge.

Unlike a traditional concert, the show allows audience members to help shape the setlist by requesting songs from an extensive catalog of classic rock favorites, creating a unique performance every night. Backed by a talented group of musicians, Weinberg delivers energetic renditions of iconic songs spanning multiple decades of rock history. Known for its interactive format, exceptional musicianship, and spontaneous atmosphere, Max Weinberg's Jukebox offers fans an engaging celebration of classic rock and live performance culture.

events.title: Beginner Woodturning: Holiday Ornaments with Matt Iannacci
events.description: Make your own ornament in time for the holiday season in this beginner-friendly workshop! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, November 7th, 2026 Time: 10am-1pm Description: In this workshop, students will learn how to create a hanging ball-and-icicle style holiday ornament using different woods to add color and texture. Great for both beginner and intermediate turners, students will learn the capabilities of spindle-orientation woodturning. Each student will walk away with at least one finished, polished ornament, ready to be displayed for the holidays! Time permitting, the instructor will also demonstrate how to turn a more advanced holiday tree-shaped ornament. Special thanks to Turners Anonymous for the use of lathes during this workshop! Tuition: $80 + $25 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided. You will be working in a fully operational woodshop and we will go over all equipment safety precautions. Please arrive wearing closed toed shoes, no loose or baggy clothing, and long hair tied back. Location: Contemporary Craft Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. If you require accessibility accommodations, please let us know by calling 412.261.7003 and we are happy to assist you. About the Artist “I have been woodturning for over 10 years, and doing wood flatwork for more than 7 years. I focus on medium-sized peices (vases, urns, etc., in woodturning, and jewelry boxes and frames in flatwork), usually seeking to combine different wood species to provide color and texture in my pieces. I am also the inventor of the JS3 jig, which is used to set up for compound-angle cuts necessary for splayed-stave woodturning, or boxes with leaning walls.” Outside of woodworking, Matt is a full-time mechanical engineer, a dad, and a saxophone and flute-player in a jazz band in the North Hills in Pittsburgh.

events.title: Basketry: French-Style Wine Basket with Traycee Bosle
events.description: Elevate your plaiting skills in this two-day workshop and create a wine basket just in time for holiday gatherings and gifting! Basketry: French-Style Wine Basket with Traycee Bosle two-day workshop Date: Saturdays November 7 and November 14 Time: 1:30 PM – 4:30 PM Description: Elevate your plaiting skills in this two-day workshop designed for students who have completed at least one basket-weaving class or who have some experiecne making a basket. Participants will explore next-level techniques, including weaving a solid basket floor, working with varying material widths, creating visual patterns with curls, and decorating a handle. Along the way, students will gain confidence in shaping and finishing more complex forms. The result is an elegant French-style wine basket that is both functional and beautiful. Size is 10 inches wide x 5 inches deep x 14 inches high. This workshop is part of our 2026 Gift Guide Suite of offerings! Make a gift to give someone special this holiday season, while giving yourself the gift of learning and camraderie in the studio! There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Traycee Bosle is a professional basket weaver at Craftisinal Creative Works—her arts studio in Pittsburgh, PA. She is a member of the Handweavers Guild of America and the Fiber Arts Guild of Pittsburgh. With over 1500 works in several different weaving styles under her belt, you can find her work in homes across the U.S. Basketweaving is an ancient art that crosses nearly all time, geographic, political, and social boundaries. It’s rooted in history, mathematics and pattern, color theory and design—with so much to offer—yet it’s nearly a lost art. Traycee has made it her mission to share her love for this once ubiquitous and critical skill with people of all ages. Her classes are fun, informative and personalized! She provides hands-on, individualized instruction using her own specially designed basket kits to teach the fundamentals of the art and meet each student where they are in their skill level. Whether you are an absolute beginner or have already made a few baskets, you will walk away with new skills and a beautiful basket you can use every day.

events.title: Introduction to Weaving: Beginner Basics with Luca Budofsky
events.description: Weaving-curious? This workshop will introduce you to various types of looms, and will get you started weaving on a frame loom! Introduction to Weaving: Beginner Basics with Jamie Boyle 3-hour workshop Date: Saturday, November 7 Time: 2:00pm – 5:00pm Description: Curious about different kinds of looms? Want to try weaving but you are not sure where to start? Let this workshop be a beginning for you! Jamie will share some weaving basics and will guide you through weaving on a frame loom, which you will get to take home with you! Additionally, you will get to experience how some different types of looms function, including a rigid heddle loom and a multi-harness loom, guided by the general question: what does a loom do? In this class you will primarily work with your hands on a non-mechanical frame loom, but you will get an overview of various modes of weaving and get to try other looms in the studio! Tuition: $65 + $15 materials fee (if you are viewing this listing on your phone, scroll down to the bottom of the page for the class registration link) Materials: all materials are included. Registration: Register through Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available—with some limitations—to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Scholarship application is found at this link . You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, TImmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the Fibers Loft on the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. About the Artist Luca Budofsky is a multimedia artist from northern New Jersey. They hold a BFA from Carnegie Mellon University School of Art with a minor in Soft Technologies. They take particular interest in how textiles occupy shifting scales of material production and the way the woven structure breaks a surface into modular interlocking pieces. They love chance encounters with light casted on walls and sidewalks. They like noise. They think public radio is cool. They attribute their interest in cyclical events and repetitive processes to being a triplet. Luca has been recognized as an Andrew Carnegie Society Scholar and as a recipient of the Samuel Rosenberg Art Award. They work and weave in Pittsburgh, PA.

events.title: JESSICA LEA MAYFIELD
events.description: JESSICA LEA MAYFIELD with support from RACHEL BOBBITT $22 ADV / $25 DOS 7PM DOORS / 8PM MUSIC ALL AGES for fans of... Squirrel Flower, Merce Lemon, Neko Case, Wild Pink BIO: When I was recording what would become “Miss Obliteration” with Day Wave I started to get the eerie sense that I was writing more than lyrics, but predictive themes. I was married to my second husband but could see the writing on the wall, a metaphorical tornado was about to tear through my life I denied it. The record kept getting pushed back for various reasons, and I kept thinking it was getting pushed back by a greater force, now 3 years later my life is entirely different and I am radically changed as a person. From my spiritual beliefs, to my person goals and dreams and just in general, nearly everything. I had a feeling this album wouldn’t see light until that chapter of my life complete.

events.title: Demi Adejuyigbe
events.description:
Join comedian, writer, and internet personality Demi Adejuyigbe for a night of stand-up comedy. Known for his viral September re-imagining music videos, his work as a writer on 'The Good Place' and 'The Late Show with Stephen Colbert,' and his popular podcast appearances, Demi brings his sharp wit and unique comedic style to the stage. Two shows will be held on November 8 at 7:00 PM and 9:30 PM.

DEMI ADEJUYIGBE returns to Bottlerocket with a is a brand-new hour of original jokes, songs and bits he has designed for the sole express purpose of abandoning his scruples and making as much money as humanly possible.

Demi made his Bottlerocket debut last year with the much heralded fringe favorite DEMI ADEJUYIGBE IS GOING TO DO ONE (1) BACKFLIP - now he returns which his follow up, also a fringe favorite from this August’s festival, DEMI ADEJUYIGBE SELLS OUT! Demi has long been one of our favorite people in comedy, and in recent years it feels like the world has finally caught up; as he’s seen his fanbase grow from Dropout to Letterboxd and beyond! If it’s like the rest of Demi’s work you can expect something deeply silly, full of archaic references and a touch of musical performance, ultimately landing somewhere much more profound experience than you may have expected. That’s what makes Demi so exciting, and that’s why we’re so excited to welcome him BACK to the Bottlerocket stage!

events.title: Donny Benet

Known for his charismatic stage persona, retro aesthetic, and tongue-in-cheek sense of humor, Benét creates music that pays homage to vintage dance grooves while maintaining a contemporary appeal. His albums, including The Don, Mr Experience, and Le Piano, showcase his talents as a bassist, producer, and songwriter, combining infectious rhythms, silky melodies, and playful storytelling. While his image often embraces irony and nostalgia, the musicianship behind his work is highly regarded, with intricate arrangements and polished production earning praise from critics and fans alike. Through energetic live performances and a catalog filled with stylish, groove-driven songs, Donny Benét has established himself as one of the most unique and entertaining figures in modern independent music.

events.title: Mountain Grass Unit
events.description: Mountain Grass Unit is a fast-rising bluegrass ensemble that has earned attention for its impressive musicianship, youthful energy, and fresh approach to traditional American roots music. The band blends the foundational elements of bluegrass—lightning-fast picking, tight harmonies, and acoustic instrumentation—with influences drawn from jam bands, folk, and contemporary Americana, creating a sound that appeals to both longtime bluegrass fans and newer audiences. Known for dynamic live performances, the group frequently stretches songs into inventive improvisational passages while maintaining the precision and craftsmanship associated with classic bluegrass traditions. Their growing reputation on the festival circuit has been fueled by a commitment to authentic musicianship and a willingness to explore new creative directions within the genre. As they continue to build a national following, Mountain Grass Unit is helping introduce a new generation of listeners to the enduring appeal of acoustic string music while carving out a distinctive identity of its own.

events.description: Learn some advanced woodturning tips and tricks while making an ornate Holiday Ornament! 2-Part Workshop Date: Tuesday, November 10th + Tuesday, November 17th, 2026 Time: 6pm-9pm, both days Description: In this two-part class, students will learn how to turn a hollow ornament with “windows” through it, framing a small tree inside. Making this ornament will help turners practice tool control, as forming small details and working with a light touch are necessary. This class is best suited for students with some experience working with a lathe. Special thanks to Turners Anonymous for the use of lathes during this workshop! I am also the inventor of the JS3 jig, which is used to set up for compound-angle cuts necessary for splayed-stave woodturning, or boxes with leaning walls.” Outside of woodworking, Matt is a full-time mechanical engineer, a dad, and a saxophone and flute-player in a jazz band in the North Hills in Pittsburgh.

events.title: SPANISH LOVE SONGS
events.description: SPANISH LOVE SONGS with support tba $20 ADV / $25 DOS 7PM DOORS / 8PM MUSIC ALL AGES for fans of... The Menzingers, The Wonder Years, The Hotelier The National Independent Venue Association (NIVA) announces the first-ever “Certified Live Independent Tour” featuring Los Angeles indie rock quintet Spanish Love Songs. The band’s 20-city tour will visit independent venues exclusively, marking the inaugural tour for the “Live Independent” certification program. NIVA developed the groundbreaking initiative to elevate and safeguard independent venues, promoters, and festivals nationwide. BIO: Over the last decade, SPANISH LOVE SONGS have watched a fiercely loyal community take shape one cramped club show and one new listener at a time. That momentum has carried the band to tours with The Wonder Years, Alkaline Trio and Hot Mulligan, along with appearances at Furnace Fest, 2000trees and the revived Vans Warped Tour, following the release of instant classics Schmaltz (2018), Brave Faces Everyone (2020) and No Joy (2023). This intimate, powerful connection with their audience is proof that even in an era defined by isolation, people are still out there yearning for others to stand beside them in the darkness. That search continues on FUTURE NAUSEA, the Pure Noise quintet's fourth LP. Drawing from the widescreen ambition of heartland rock – the anthemic sweep of records like Born in the U.S.A., Sam's Town and Full Moon Fever – shimmering synths, ringing guitars and soaring choruses define an expansive sound crafted across sessions with producers Chris Walla (Death Cab for Cutie) and Sarah Tudzin (Illuminati Hotties). Against that backdrop, Dylan Slocum's characteristically observational lyricism remains the band’s beating heart: deeply empathetic and unflinchingly honest as he chronicles political violence, climate anxiety, late-stage capitalism and the quiet ways these existential crises seep into everyday life – and, just as critically, how moments of love, companionship and shared resilience become the antidote to an increasingly uncertain future.

Plus, visit our sensory table and explore our Interactive Play Spaces, including a larger-than-life Draw Alive station. Sensory Bags from KultureCity, featuring items like headphones and fidget toys, are available to borrow daily at the National Aviary.A helpful sensory guide to the sights, sounds, and climate of the Aviary's habitats can be viewed in advance AND during your trip. Please register in advance!

events.title: JOSH GONDLEMAN
events.description: Josh Gondelman is a writer and comedian who incubated in Boston before moving to New York City, where he currently lives and most recently worked as the head writer and an executive producer for Desus & Mero on Showtime. Previously, he spent five years at Last Week Tonight with John Oliver, first as a web producer and then as a staff writer where he earned four Emmy Awards, two Peabody Awards, and three WGA Awards. Josh also previously wrote for Fuse TV’s Billy On The Street. Why'd We Book It? Josh is an incledibly silly guy with a calm voice that brings all the wit and self deprication that makes you laugh. We love seeing him on Wait Wait... Don't Tell Me! - he is a hilarious panelist and it is always a treat when they have him. As fans, we also had a blast watching John Oliver and being able to pin point what jokes were written by Josh For Fans Of... Tommy Brennan, Caleb Hearon, Joe Pera Extended Bio: His most recent hour, Positive Reinforcement, is now available to stream. Josh’s debut standup special People Pleaser was released in 2022. In 2016, Josh made his late-night standup debut on Conan (TBS), and he has also performed on Late Night With Seth Meyers (NBC) and The Late Late Show with James Corden (CBS). Gondelman is the author of the essay collection Nice Try: Stories of Best Intentions and Mixed Results published September 2019 by Harper Perennial. Since 2019, he has been a regular panelist on NPR mainstay Wait Wait Don’t Tell Me. Offstage, Gondelman is also the co-author (along with Joe Berkowitz) of the book You Blew It, published October 2015 by Plume. events.description: The Winter Tales immersive experience is back by popular demand, transforming the McKenna Gallery into a sensory journey through a magical winter world!Created by award-winning OLO Creative Farm, this one-of-a-kind installation brings to life stunning works from The Westmoreland’s collection using multi-projection, surround sound, and delicate animated effects like mist, falling snow, and glistening frost. Featuring artists such as William Coventry Wall, Charles W. (Bud) Gibbons, Henry Koerner, and Ron Donoughe, the experience seamlessly blends art and technology. Visitors will feel as though they’ve stepped inside the paintings, surrounded by winter landscapes from Greensburg, Pittsburgh, the countryside, and beyond.Select original winter works from the collection are also on view.On view during regular Museum hours. Admission is free; no reservation required.

events.title: Member Preview: Greer Lankton: "Could It Be Love"
events.description: Greer Lankton: Could It Be LoveCurated by Francis Schichtel and Jordan WeitzmanCould It Be Love presents an intimate and powerful photographic survey of Greer Lankton (1958–1996), the legendary East Village artist known for her uncannily lifelike dolls and fearless exploration of gender, beauty, and the body. Featuring 24 rarely seen photographs of her iconic dolls, taken by Lankton herself, this exhibition reveals her uncanny ability to imbue life into her sculpted figures as they lounge, gossip, and perform across New York’s gritty and gorgeous downtown scene.This exhibition celebrates Lankton not only as a trailblazing trans artist but also as a completely original image-maker whose lens captured a world of oddballs, queer icons, and doll-like doppelgängers with equal parts glamour, melancholy, and wit. Presented in partnership with Magic Hour Press, Could It Be Love follows the release of the first major monograph on Lankton’s photographic work.Discover the new exhibition, then mingle with fellow members over light refreshments in the lobby.Not a member yet? Support the museum today and gain access to special events all year long.Please note, parking is limited at our main lot at 505 Jacksonia Street, with additional street parking available in the surrounding neighborhood. About Greer LanktonGreer Lankton (1958 – 1996) was one of the most significant artists to have taken part in the revolutionary art scene of New York City’s East Village during the 1980s. Lankton grew up in Park Forest, IL, where she graduated a year early from high school to attend the Art Institute of Chicago from 1975 to1978. That year she moved to New York City and received her BFA from Pratt Institute in 1981. By then Lankton had secured her reputation as a leading figure in the social ferment of NYC in the 1980s through her visceral doll sculpture, and now lesser-known performances and minimalist soft sculpture.Lankton’s drawings are frequently compared to that of the expressionist Egon Schiele and her dolls and their photographic portraits, to that of surrealist Hans Bellmer. Yet her experimental and multimedia work are located within a history of transfeminism, avant-garde performance and even pop-art, while at the same time is equally situated within a neo-punk canon and the Trash Trilogy of John Waters films - Pink Flamingos being her favorite.Lankton’s exhibitions and performances included those at PS1, Club 57, Pyramid Club, Franklyn Furnace, Civilian Warfare Gallery, Hal Bromm and the Whitney Biennale, NYC. She also exhibited across the US and Europe, including the UK, Austria and the Venice Biennale, Italy. She exhibited her first full-scale installation artwork at the Mattress Factory Museum shortly before her untimely death in 1996. About the monograph Could It Be LoveEdited by Nan Goldin, Francis Schichtel, and Jordan Weitzman, the book draws deeply from the Greer Lankton Archive, housed at Mattress Factory, to present over 100 of Lankton’s rarely seen photographs. These images offer an intimate and theatrical glimpse into Lankton’s inner world, one populated by glamorous oddballs, downtown legends, and avatars of her own making.This exhibition is made possible by Teiger Foundation.

events.title: Birding Expedition: Blue Spruce County Park
events.description: Sat., November 14 | 8:30 - 11:30 amMembers: $50; Non-Members: $55 Meet Blue Spruce County Park Make your own magical woodland moment come to life with a trip to Blue Spruce County Park. Meet up with National Aviary Educator and Photographer Mike Faix and Ornithologist Robert Mulvihill for a morning of birdwatching...and chickadee feeding! Birders and animal-lovers will be able to hone bird identification skills, while younger families with birding beginners can learn the basics as you explore one of Western Pennsylvania’s most beautiful locations.Join us for this very special Indiana County birding experience, where adorable chickadees have been taught to land on the outstretched fingertips of bird watchers of all ages for scrumptious sunflower seeds! Having birds land on your hand for a seasonal snack is a very special and memorable experience for ALL ages that you don’t want to miss! Of course, November is near the height of fall bird migration, so Bob and Mike will also lead you on a park exploration in search of waterfowl and other traveling species. Both experts are experienced birding and education expert who will be able to provide interesting information and birding tales appealing to kids and adults alike. Birding Expeditions are open to participants 6 years and older. Those under 18 must be accompanied by a registered adult. Bring your own binoculars, or borrow an Aviary pair that we'll help you use!

events.title: The Whiskey Smash
events.description: This annual celebration of Pennsylvania rye whiskey welcomes distilleries from across the state to historic West Overton Village!17 Pennsylvania distilleries will be set up on two floors of the Museum (the former 1859 distillery building) providing samples, sharing knowledge about their brands, and selling products. Additionally, samples of Overholt™ will be available in the Overholt Stateroom.Along with the whiskey, enjoy a meal from Mission BBQ, bespoke chocolates from Scottdale Chocolate Company, and our signature Whiskey Smash cocktail. Dinner, chocolates, and cocktails will all be located in the Overholt Room, the lower level of the Museum.VIP Admissions also receive an early VIP hour from 5 - 6 p.m., which includes an exclusive Overholt™ personalized limited release sampling with one of three educators available only during the VIP hour in the Stateroom. Additionally, VIPs can enjoy a VIP Curated Cocktail during the VIP hour along with the Whiskey Smash Cocktail downstairs in the Overholt Room. Explore the James B. Beam Pennsylvania Whiskey Heritage Center, a fully renovated and redesigned floor of our Museum that honors the past, present and future of Pennsylvania whiskey. Browse the largest publicly accessible collection of Pennsylvania whiskey artifacts in the Sam Komlenic Gallery, which includes 270+ historic whiskey bottles.Enjoy samples of Overholt™ in the Overholt Stateroom, the vintage-inspired lounge that pays homage to the origins of Overholt™ whiskey at West Overton. Overholt™ is recognized by whiskey historians as the longest standing American whiskey brand with an unbroken chain of ownership, production and sale since Abraham Overholt began distilling at West Overton in 1810. While the brand is produced today by James B. Beam Distilling Co. in Clermont, Kentucky, West Overton is proud to be the “spiritual home” of Overholt™.The Whiskey Smash is a fundraiser benefiting the nonprofit mission of West Overton Village. Our historic site, museum, and educational distillery invite visitors to discover the heritage of whiskey production at West Overton and across Pennsylvania. Proceeds from the Whiskey Smash support efforts including educational programs and historic preservation.This event is for ages 21+ with valid ID only. All guests must present a valid ID at the door, regardless of age. Guests without a valid ID will not be able to enter and tickets will not be refunded. Get TicketsGet your tickets here! Participating DistilleriesBig Springs SpiritsBurgess & Burgess DistilleryDad's HatDisobedient SpiritsGrumpy Goat DistilleryHeist SpiritsIron City Distilling / Bessemer Rye Kinsey Distilling Co. Liberty Pole SpiritsMeadville Distilling / Conneaut CellarsPark Family Farms DistilleryPonfeigh DistilleryRed Pump SpiritsStoll & WolfeTall Pines DistilleryWest Overton DistillingWigle Whiskey Plan your visitThe event is hosted at the Museum at West Overton Village, 109 W. Overton Road, Scottdale, PA. Please note accessing the Heritage Center requires stairs as we fundraise for an elevator. Contact us to discuss accessibility concerns.

events.title: Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre, Pointe in Time Gala
events.description: Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre (PBT)’s Pointe in Time fundraiser is a top 10 annual event that brings over 400 arts patrons together in support of PBT’s mainstage programming, arts education in schools and community centers, classes for individuals with disabilities, and funding for its Bridge Scholarship program. Scholarships cover all tuition costs (school year and summer) as well as associated costs (pointe shoes, leotards and tights) which can cost up to $70,000 per student.For 57 years, Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre has inspired our community and made it a more beautiful place – on the stage, in the studio and in our neighborhoods. Join us in celebrating PBT’s Season of Wonder!The evening includes a multi-course dining experience for guests as they enjoy exclusive world-premiere performances by PBT company artists and PBT School students. A silent and live auction, pointe shoe raffle, and dancing are all a part of the night’s festivities.We invite you to gather family, friends, colleagues and clients, and join us for an unforgettable night celebrating PBT’s world-class art and life-changing programs.

events.title: Orpheus & Eurydice
events.description: After the death of his beloved Eurydice, Orpheus vows to plunge into the very depths of the Underworld itself to bring her back. Moved by Orpheus’s passion, Amore (Cupid) appears and agrees to aid him in the rescue of his wife so long as he does not look at her until they return to the land of the living again.With the help of the spirits of the Underworld, Orpheus finds Eurydice in Elysium. But as he guides her to the surface, he knows he cannot look back. Eurydice believes this means he does not love her, and she refuses to take another step until he looks her way. So he does… but this classic tale may not end the way you’ve seen before!Based on the same Greek myth that inspired the Broadway hit Hadestown, Christoph Willibald Gluck's original 1774 score is enhanced by Hector Berlioz’s 1859 re-arrangement, making this a story that has only been enriched over the centuries.NOVEMBER 14, 20, 22, 2026 These performances are sponsored in part by The Gailliot Fund.

events.title: Yaelokre - Keath Osk
events.description: Yaelokre is the musical storytelling project of Icelandic-Filipino singer-songwriter and multimedia artist Keath Ósk. Built around the illustrated, diary-turned-storybook world of “Meadowlark,” the project follows the Lark, a quartet of young minstrels, through folk-inspired songs and character-driven mythology. Yaelokre gained broad attention with “Harpy Hare,” followed by releases including “And the Hound,” “Hartebeest,” and the “Composing Colentine” EP. Ósk’s work combines songwriting, illustration, and fairytale world-building into a distinctive contemporary folk presentation.
