events.title: The Menzingers with Hot Water Music and Weakened Friends
events.description: The Menzingers are a punk rock band known for emotionally driven songwriting, anthemic choruses, and a sound that blends punk energy with heartland rock and Americana influences. Their music often explores nostalgia, aging, friendship, heartbreak, and everyday struggles through relatable storytelling and melodic guitar-driven arrangements. Known for passionate live performances and singalong-ready songs, the band has built a devoted following within the punk and alternative rock communities. With a balance of raw emotion and high-energy musicianship, The Menzingers have become one of the defining bands in modern punk rock.Hot Water Music is a post-hardcore and punk band recognized for gritty vocals, emotionally charged songwriting, and a melodic yet aggressive sound rooted in punk rock tradition. Their music combines driving rhythms, dual vocal harmonies, and themes of perseverance, resilience, and personal reflection that have resonated with fans for decades. Known for powerful live performances and a strong underground legacy, Hot Water Music remains one of the most influential bands in melodic punk and post-hardcore music.Weakened Friends is an alternative rock trio known for fuzzy guitar tones, sharp songwriting, and a blend of indie rock, punk, and grunge-inspired energy. Their music balances catchy melodies with emotionally honest lyrics and explosive instrumentation that creates a raw and energetic live-show atmosphere. With a sound rooted in modern indie rock while embracing punk attitude and emotional vulnerability, Weakened Friends continues to gain attention as a rising force in alternative music.

events.title: THE OLD ALLEGHENY COUNTY JAIL AND MUSEUM-FREE
events.description: Open on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of the month except on Court holidays.Visit at your convenience between 11:30 am and 1:00 pm--Cost: FREEPHLF docents are on hand to tell you the story of the former Allegheny County Jail. Completed in 1886 to the designs of Boston architect H.H. Richardson, it closed on July 27, 1995. The building was then renovated between 1995 and 2001 and adapted for a new use as the Family Division of the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas. Working with the leadership of Allegheny County and with funding from the Drue Heinz Trust, our organization coordinated with the former jail's Deputy Warden Ed Urban and the Allegheny County Juvenile Court to preserve one portion of the cell blocks of the historic jail to create the Old Allegheny County Jail Museum. The Jail Museum, located in Downtown--at 440 Ross Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15219--opened in 2005.To access the Museum: Enter the Family Court Building through the main entrance on Ross Street. You will then be processed through a security checkpoint. The Museum is located across from the vending machine room. The use of cameras is NOT permitted.

events.description: Clown Boss Chad Damiani live directs a group of comics through their very first clown show. Along the way, he ruthlessly teases, cajoles and drives them to abandon their intellect and follow their dumbest impulses. A glorious celebration of failure and the cruelest show in clown, CHAD is BACK at Bottlerocket for another one-of-a-kind show you won't want to miss. Why'd We Book It? Clowning has sweeped the comedy world. Ask anyone who knows and they'll tell you who the real American CLOWN BOSS is - CHAD DAMIANI! Here's an opportunity to see the peak of a newly hot artform - and perhaps it's best teacher instructing LIVE ON STAGE (and being funny, don't worry) Extended Bio: CLOWN BOSS Chad Damiani is one of the architects of LA’s modern clown scene. He’s the creator/star of the STAND UP AND CLOWN podcast and live show – where he directs comics through their first clown performance. He’s an ensemble member for the international clown variety show STAMPTOWN (which just secured a Netflix comedy special for 2026). He has made numerous appearances on TV and film – including AGT, DAVE and TBS’s recent reboot of JO SCHMO. Chad works as a clown consultant for various artists and organizations – including Spiegelworld, Natalie Palamides and Piff the Magic Dragon. events.title: WYEP Presents: Aaron Lee Tasjan w/ Madeleine Kelson
events.description: WYEP PRESENTS: https://wyep.org/Doors 7PM | Show 8PM$25 ADV | $30 DOS21+Aaron Lee Tasjan was experiencing the worst bout of imposter syndrome of his career when he sat down and wrote Todd Snider a vulnerable email asking for advice. Tasjan, despite writing and recording some of the most astute Americana rock songs of the last decade and being nominated for a Grammy, just didnt see a future for an independent singer, songwriter, and guitarist like himself.Snider read Tasjans email and immediately replied: I think I have some ideas. Ill write you back tomorrow.The next morning, Tasjan awoke to a signature Todd Snider missive for how to move forward as an artist. It was a novel-length email that read like the battle plans for the Invasion of Normandy. Do this, Snider wrote. Then this. But never that. The specifics dont matter besides, thatd be giving away the secret but Tasjan devoured his mentors words and took them to heart.He began writing feverishly, unbothered by expectations and immune to any pressure to match his acclaimed albums like In the Blazes, Karma for Cheap, or his most recent, 2024s Stellar Evolution. When he was through, Tasjan had Get Over It, Underdog, his most inspiring LP to date. Produced by Tasjan and his longtime sound engineer Mark Miller, the album is a celebration of the power of songwriting, the unbreakable bond of friendship, and the determination of the dark horse.I went to the ultimate oasis for a singer, songwriter, and troubadour: Todd Snider. And he said, in very Todd fashion, You can find your path forward by going backwards, Tasjan says with a laugh. But he was right. I set aside my ego, played shows solo without my band, and wrote a lot of songs. In that process, I found my confidence again.Tragically, however, he lost his mentor. Snider died shortly after Get Over It, Underdog, was finished, leaving a void in the folk-rock scene that will prove nearly impossible to fill. But Tasjan is committed to carrying on Sniders unbridled spirit and lifting up underdogs everywhere.Over 11 tracks, Tasjans new album kills sacred cows and pokes holes in the dam, while leaning hard into the idea of perseverance. In the talking-blues of Science Friction, he tells an abridged origin story of civilization that culminates with humankind editing itself out of its own picture. Man made machines/putting man out of business, he sings witha knowing wink. Lost meanwhile, finds him feeling like a stranger in this town. Its a compact blast of indie-rock with a sing-along chorus that underscores Tasjans gift for writing infectious hooks.

events.title: Beartooth w/ Don Broco
events.description: Beartooth is a powerhouse hard rock and metalcore band founded by vocalist, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Caleb Shomo, whose intensely personal approach to music has helped the group build a devoted international following. Known for blending aggressive riffs, massive choruses, and honest lyrics that address mental health, self-improvement, and resilience, Beartooth has earned acclaim through albums such as Disgusting, Disease, Below, and The Surface.Joining them on this tour is Don Broco, a British rock band celebrated for its genre-defying sound that combines alternative rock, electronic influences, infectious hooks, and a dynamic sense of experimentation. Magnolia Park adds a fresh perspective with its energetic fusion of pop-punk, alternative rock, hip-hop, and modern pop influences, creating a style that appeals to a broad new generation of listeners.Opening the lineup is Australia's Windwaker, a rapidly rising act known for incorporating metalcore, electronic elements, and cinematic production into emotionally charged songs that showcase both technical skill and creative ambition. Together, these four bands deliver a diverse and high-energy concert experience that highlights the evolving landscape of modern rock and heavy music while offering something unique for fans across multiple genres.

events.title: Goose
events.description: Goose is an American jam band known for its vibrant improvisation, polished musicianship, and ability to blend rock, funk, folk, electronic, and indie influences into expansive live performances. Formed in Connecticut, the group built a passionate following through constant touring, word-of-mouth buzz, and fan-shared recordings that showcased the unpredictability and energy of its concerts. Their songs often begin with memorable melodies and tight arrangements before opening into adventurous instrumental passages that make each performance feel distinct from the last. Albums such as Dripfield and Everything Must Go have helped introduce Goose to a wider audience while preserving the exploratory spirit that first drew fans to the band. With a reputation for marathon sets, dynamic stage chemistry, and a steadily growing national presence, Goose has become one of the most talked-about acts in the modern jam-band scene.

events.title: Intro to Blacksmithing: Campfire Forks with Eleanor Davidson
events.description: Learn how to forge your very own campfire fork! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Thursday, November 19th Time: 6pm- 9pm Description: Participants will learn basic blacksmithing techniques including chiseling, tapering, flattening, and twisting to create a 20″ long camping fork, great for roasting hot dogs or marshmallows over a fire. Beginner friendly and open to all skill levels! This class will involve hot metal, fire, and repetitive swinging of a hammer, it will be somewhat physically demanding so slight stamina is required. You’ll leave this class with a finished campfire fork of your very own! Tuition: $80+ $30 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided. Students should wear natural fibers such as cotton and denim. Uncuffed pants and closed-toe shoes are required (no shorts or sandals permitted). Long hair should be restrained. Safety glasses and hearing protection are provided; however, participants may bring their own if preferred. We recommend bringing a water bottle to stay hydrated. This workshop is in an open air studio, bring a coat to keep warm before the forges get fired up! Location: Contemporary Craft – Timmons Studios, Blacksmithing Studio (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. We are unable to refund materials cost for this workshop. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Eleanor Davidson is an artist, fabricator, and educator hailing from Kentucky and currently based in Pittsburgh, PA. Her work honors traditional craft techniques and industrial processes, primarily through metal casting, blacksmithing, and quilting. Prior to landing in Pittsburgh, Davidson was a longtime beginner blacksmithing instructor with the Kentucky Forge Council and Appalachian Area Chapter of Blacksmiths, and a featured demonstrator with the Kentucky Folklife Program. She holds a BFA in Sculpture from Western Kentucky University.

events.title: Cosmic Microwave Background
events.description:
Cosmic Microwave Background by Julia Fraser is a full-length play that shakes the anxieties of the digital age. Rita, a translator of Italian poetry, and her husband leave New York for remote calm in the desert. But after they arrive, only she hears a snaking sound that envelops the landscape and punctures her fresh start. When her tech-optimist neighbor echoes her interest in what she hears, they set off to uncover the noise before it explodes her sanity. It propels her on a quest to find its elusive source and recover her stability. How’s your hearing?

events.title: Motionless In White with Dayseeker, The Devil Wears Prada and Dark Divine
events.description: Motionless In White is a metalcore band known for combining crushing heaviness, gothic imagery, industrial influences, and cinematic songwriting into a distinctive modern metal sound. Fronted by Chris Motionless, the band explores themes of individuality, resilience, horror aesthetics, and self-empowerment through powerful vocals and dramatic arrangements. Their music seamlessly blends aggressive breakdowns, electronic elements, and memorable choruses, helping them become one of the most recognizable acts in contemporary heavy music. Known for visually striking live performances and an unwavering connection with fans, Motionless In White continues to push the boundaries of modern metal.Dayseeker is a post-hardcore and alternative rock band celebrated for emotionally charged songwriting, atmospheric soundscapes, and the soulful vocals of Rory Rodriguez. Their music balances vulnerability and intensity, exploring themes of love, grief, mental health, healing, and personal transformation. Blending melodic rock, ambient textures, and modern production, Dayseeker has developed a sound that resonates deeply with listeners seeking both emotional depth and musical sophistication. Their captivating live performances have helped establish them as one of the most respected bands in the modern alternative scene.The Devil Wears Prada is a metalcore band known for its relentless energy, technical musicianship, and willingness to evolve beyond traditional genre boundaries. Their music combines aggressive riffs, dynamic vocal interplay, and thought-provoking lyrics that often explore personal struggles, perseverance, and human emotion. Over the years, the band has incorporated elements of post-hardcore, progressive metal, and atmospheric rock while maintaining the intensity that first earned them acclaim. Renowned for powerful live shows and a consistently innovative approach, The Devil Wears Prada remains a major force in heavy music.Dark Divine is a modern rock and metal band recognized for blending dark theatrical aesthetics with melodic metalcore and alternative metal influences. Their music features dramatic atmospheres, heavy instrumentation, and emotionally driven lyrics that explore themes of inner conflict, identity, heartbreak, and self-discovery. Combining haunting melodies with explosive energy, the band creates a sound that appeals to fans of both modern metal and gothic-inspired rock. Known for captivating performances and a strong visual identity, Dark Divine continues to gain attention as an emerging presence in the contemporary heavy music scene.

Their artistry lives on in *Love Letter from the Afterlife*, a multimedia presentation built around Gibson’s final filmed live performance. The experience combines film, live poetry, music, orchestral accompaniment, and intimate storytelling, with Megan Falley sharing personal reflections on Gibson’s life and creative legacy. It offers audiences a moving, immersive celebration of a singular voice whose poetry transformed the modern spoken-word experience.

events.title: Kelsey Waldon
events.description: Doors 7PM | Show 8PM $25 ADV | $30 DOS 21+ Waldon's fearlessness is among the reasons she landed at Oh Boy Records in 2019, as the independent label's first new signee in 15 years. It's attracted fans to her headline tours and her festival sets, and prompted artists including Tyler Childers, Charley Crockett, Robert Earl Keen, Margo Price, and Lucinda Williams to invite her on tour. It helped earn her both the title of , "rdquo" -> Kentucky Colonel" --- an honor recognizing goodwill ambassadors of Kentucky's culture and traditions --- and a spot in the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum's annual American Currents exhibit in 2024. , "rdquo" -> True outlaw shit is sticking to your guns, and I feel like I'm doing that," Waldon says. , "rdquo" -> I'm not saying I'm unbreakable, but I feel almost unbreakable. I've already hurt the worst that I could and lived to tell the story. We can be thankful for our ghosts."

events.title: Completely Unchained - Van Halen Tribute
events.description: Completely Unchained is a Van Halen tribute band focused on the group’s classic 1978–1984 era. The four-piece lineup features Gene Henriksen on vocals, Jake C. Miller on guitar, Clint Ettore on bass and Ronnie Sciascia on drums. Its repertoire includes Van Halen staples such as “Jump,” “Panama,” “Ain’t Talkin’ ’Bout Love” and “Hot for Teacher,” alongside deeper cuts. The band’s presentation emphasizes Van Halen’s signature guitar tones, soaring harmonies, driving rhythms and high-energy stage style.

events.title: Zack Fox - DJ (18 and Over)
events.description: Zack Fox is a comedian, rapper, writer, actor, and internet personality whose unpredictable humor and fearless creativity have made him one of the most distinctive entertainers of his generation. First gaining widespread attention through his viral social media presence and sharp comedic commentary, Fox has successfully expanded into stand-up comedy, music, television, and voice acting while cultivating a devoted fan base. His stand-up performances blend surreal observations, improvisation, pop culture references, and personal stories into a fast-paced, anything-can-happen experience that keeps audiences constantly surprised. In addition to comedy, Fox has earned recognition for his music and creative collaborations, showcasing a versatility that allows him to move effortlessly between different forms of entertainment without losing his unmistakable comedic voice. Whether performing onstage, recording music, or creating digital content, Zack Fox delivers an energetic, unconventional, and thoroughly original performance that reflects his unique perspective and boundless imagination.

events.title: Metal Clay Bird Whistle with Donna Penoyer
events.description: Learn how to work with silver metal clay while making a custom bird whistle! All-Day Workshop Date: Saturday, November 21st, 2026 Time: 10am-5pm Description: Make a silver bird that really sings! Learn to make a whistle pendant in the shape of a tiny bird from fine silver metal clay. The class will cover how a whistle works, including important troubleshooting tips and tricks, and will introduce the teacher’s favorite hollow-form construction technique for metal clay. Students will finish one project up to the point of firing and will leave pendants for the teacher to fire after class. Tuition: $105 + $65 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Please fill out the application here ; you can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. Location: Contemporary Craft – Raphael Building (5645 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. If you require accessibility accommodations, please let us know by calling 412.261.7003 and we are happy to assist you. About the Artist Donna Penoyer is a master metal clay instructor who has been working in the medium since 2005. She has taught workshops throughout the U.S., England, and Belgium and has created a number of video tutorials available through craftcast.com . Although she developed a spirited, over-the-top, 21-year career as a professional stiltwalker, these days Donna is pretty down-to-earth. She is a welcoming teacher who believes there is a gleeful maker in everyone.

events.title: Introduction to Improv Embroidery with Alison Stein
events.description: Create an improvisational embroidery piece, taking a "doodle approach" to stitches! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, November 21 Time: 2 – 5 pm Description: This workshop will provide gentle encouragement and instruction on how to create beautiful embroidery pieces using an unplanned, improvisational approach. Whether you have never picked up a needle or are an experienced embroiderer, this method is available to you. Enjoy the beauty of color, textile and fiber without any stress of “messing up,” which is simply impossible in this approach! Techniques and Skills covered in this class will include: Learning (or unlearning) the mindset of embroidery without a pattern. Sourcing, selecting and preparing fabric and fiber for improv embroidery. Taking a “doodle approach” to embroidery stitches. We will take a different approach to learning or re-learning the basic embroidery stitches, encouraging beginners to feel confident, and more advanced students will have a new way of thinking about and building on stitches they already know. Thinking about color choices and composition Methods for addressing results you don’t love. Tuition: $65 + $15 materials fee Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available-with some limitations- to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Fill out the scholarship application here , and you can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Materials: All materials will be provided, however, participants are encouraged to bring any tools that they need to aid in seeing up-close: reading glasses, magnifyers, etc… Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Alison J. Stein is an artist, teacher and writer based in Carnegie, PA, in the Pittsburgh metro area. She makes vibrant textile art, paintings, prints and book art, and enjoys blurring the boundaries between traditional techniques and contemporary art.

events.title: WYEP Presents: Charlie Parr
events.description: WYEP Presents:https://wyep.org/Sat Nov 21st Doors 7PM | Show 8PM$25 ADV | $30 DOS21+ Rolling Stone has called Charlie Parrs music a gritty blend of Delta blues and Depression-era roots music soaked in his hardscrabble voice. Its a sacred realm of folk wisdom and sorrowful vulnerability. NPR said he offers expertly-picked resonator guitar and lyrics that puncture the soul. Parr tours prolifically, and has performed at tastemaker events like the Newport Folk Fest and Pickathon.The Duluth-based guitarist, songwriter, and interpreter of traditional music has released twenty albums over two-and-a-half decades and has been known to perform up to 275 shows a year. Parr is a folk troubadour in the truest sense: taking to the road between shows, writing and rewriting songs as he plays, fueled by a belief that music is eternal and cannot be claimed or adequately explained. The sounds from his working-class upbringingincluding Folkways legends such as Lead Belly and Woody Guthrieimbue Parrs music with stylistic echoes of blues and folk icons of decades past. Parr sees himself merely as a continuer of a folk tradition.Parrs mastery of his craft is only more apparent when contextualized within the history of folk tradition to which Parr has dedicated his practice. The land and lives around and intersecting with Parr have always influenced him, from the hills and valleys of Hollandale, Minnesota to the Depression-era stories from his father.Parrs first album with Smithsonian Folkways, Last of the Better Days Ahead (2021), foregrounded his lyrical craftsmanship and sophisticated bluesman confidence, with spare production highlighting Parrs mastery of guitar and elevating his blues poetry. In his 2024 release, Little Sun, Parr weaved together stories celebrating music, community, and communing with nature. In doing so, he put forth an ambitious and raw album that exemplifies the best of Parrs sound: his blend of the blues and folk traditions with the steadfast originality of a poet. Now, he continues that tradition with 2026s poignant and timely Rooming House, which joins the chorus of WPA-era socially-conscious folk operas and outlaw country concept albums of the 1970s to poignantly allegorize his experiences and the experiences of the people around him.

events.title: SkyWatch Junior: Growing up with Stars
events.description: Explore the life cycle of stars and how they age with Quasi! Create your own constellation using markers, stickers, and gemstones, play with magnifying glasses to identify different objects, and explore filters and how they capture different energies of light in space. Enjoy an iconic planetarium show and stargaze from our observatory deck (weather-permitting). Viewing targets include Orion Nebula, a stellar nursery in constellation Orion, Pleiades an open star cluster located about 440 light-years away in the constellation Taurus, the Moon, and Saturn.

events.description: Jim Brickman is a pianist, composer, and songwriter known for his soothing contemporary instrumental music and romantic piano melodies. His performances blend classical influences with pop and adult contemporary styles, creating elegant compositions that are widely associated with relaxation, romance, and emotional reflection. With graceful piano work, warm stage presence, and decades of successful touring and recordings, Jim Brickman remains one of the most recognizable artists in contemporary instrumental music.

events.title: And A Buoy
events.description: And a Buoy by Eli Plummer is a staged reading about a father, a son, and a bond buoyed through the changing tides of time. Set entirely on a cuddy boat off the coast of Maine, the story anchors Sean and his son, Aaron, during their annual fishing trips. As the scenes jump from the early 2000s into the mid-2030s, the audience watches Aaron grow up, and Sean grow older. Exploring the complexities of fatherhood, the piece reveals how their connection holds strong as they navigate what love is supposed to look like—and the quiet ways it shows up.

events.title: Stephen Wilson Jr with Kashus Culpepper
events.description: Stephen Wilson Jr. with Kashus Culpepper brings together two rising artists known for emotionally driven songwriting and a fresh approach to modern Americana and country music. Stephen Wilson Jr. blends country, rock, folk, and alternative influences into a raw and deeply personal sound filled with introspective lyrics, gritty vocals, and powerful storytelling. His music often explores themes of identity, resilience, heartbreak, and personal growth through stripped-down authenticity and emotionally intense performances.Kashus Culpepper adds a soulful Southern sound rooted in country, blues, and Americana traditions, pairing heartfelt songwriting with rich vocals and organic instrumentation. His performances emphasize emotional honesty and roots-inspired musicianship that complements the raw energy of the headlining act. Together, the lineup creates a moving live music experience filled with heartfelt storytelling, Americana grit, and modern country soul.

events.title: Daily Bread
events.description: Daily Bread is the electronic project of Atlanta producer Rhett Whatley, blending vintage soul, gritty hip-hop, jazz-inspired textures, and bass-forward production into a distinctive electro-soul sound. Known for crate-digging sensibilities and richly layered live arrangements, he has grown from an underground favorite into a defining voice in contemporary bass music. His latest album, Vanishing Point, expands that palette with immersive, road-trip-inspired compositions and collaborations with artists including Late Night Radio and STS. A Daily Bread performance offers a dynamic meeting point between beat-driven energy, soulful sampling, and forward-thinking electronic production.

events.title: The Stray Cats
events.address: The Palace Theatre, 21 West Otterman Street, Greensburg, Pennsylvania 15601
events.description: The Stray Cats are an American rockabilly trio formed by guitarist-vocalist Brian Setzer, bassist Lee Rocker and drummer Slim Jim Phantom. Known for reviving 1950s-style rockabilly with a distinctive visual style and modern rock energy, the group became prominent in the early 1980s. Their self-titled 1981 album produced “Runaway Boys,” “Rock This Town” and “Stray Cat Strut,” with the latter two becoming American Top 10 hits. Other recognizable songs include “(She’s) Sexy + 17.”

events.title: Species Spotlight: Penguins
events.description: Thurs., December 3 | 2 - 4 pm | 18+Members: $25; Non-Members: $30What tuxedoed bird is known for waddling and swimming...NOT flight? The National Aviary’s African Penguin colony is a favorite of visitors and staff alike. But did you know that this charming bird is a fierce aquatic predator...one who the Aviary works with in the wild as the species is at serious risk of extinction by the year 2035? During this in-depth class for adults, learn more about African Penguins and the conservation challenges they face. Learn from an Aviary expert who leads the Saving Animals from Extinction African Penguin program. They will share the threats to African Penguins and how we are part of a team, including people from North America, South Africa, and Namibia who are working together tirelessly to save them...while we still can.This program is designed specifically for an adult learner audience. Participants must be 18 years or older to participate.

events.title: Needle Felting: Bird of the Month: Northern Cardinal with Erin Carlson
events.description: December’s bird of the month: Northern Cardinal! Learn to needle felt, while enjoying a detailed look at this fascinating bird! 3-hour workshop Date: Thursday, December 3 Time: 6pm-9pm Description: Learn to needle felt or sharpen your skills while creating your own Northern Cardinal . Fiber artist and backyard bird enthusiast Erin Carlson of Red Cottage Fiber Studio will guide you through the needle felting process as you look closely to observe the shape and markings of the species and gain a deeper appreciation of our avian neighbors. Adventurous beginners welcome. Please note that we will be using sharp needles and repetitive, detailed hand motions. About the 2026-27 Bird of the Month Needle Felting Series : Due to popular demand, Contemporary Craft is thrilled to once again partner with instructor Erin Carlson to offer this series of workshops! While first offered virtually during the pandemic, this year will be live and in-person! Classes will occur the first Thursday of each month from 6-9pm and run from March 2026-February 2027. Join us for as many classes as you like. Choose your favorite bird or join us for all 12 to complete your very own flock. The bird selections are as follows: March: American Robin April: Scarlet Tanager May: Barn Swallow June: Eastern Bluebird July: Ruby-Throated Hummingbird August: American Goldfinch September: Downy Woodpecker October: Barn Owl November: Chickadee December: Northern Cardinal January(2027): Red Breasted Nuthatch February(2027): Red Winged Blackbird Tuition: $65 + $10 materials fee (per workshop) (if you are viewing this listing on your phone, scroll down to the bottom of the page for the class registration link) Materials: all materials are included. Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Scholarship application is found at this link . You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, TImmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the Fibers Loft on the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. About the Artist Erin Carlson is a multidiscplinary fiber artist working and teaching in th Pittsburgh area for the last decade. She loves to help students explore their creativity through the use of fibers.

events.title: Aiden Sinclair in Fate & Futility: A Show of Magick & Mysteries
events.description: Join Aiden Sinclair for an esoteric evening of supernatural magic as he explores the concepts of fate and destiny in an interactive 90-minute presentation of the strange.Audiences will enjoy a storied evening of ancient magical effects that include experiences with the Tarot, Rune Casting and Prognostication that will leave all to wonder if fate might be more than an idea, and that destiny may indeed be real.Aiden Sinclair has performed as the resident Magus of the Historic Stanley Hotel in Estes Park, Colorado for over a decade where he is the proprietor of Aiden Sinclair’s Magick Underground.He has appeared on America’s Got Talent and Penn & Teller: Fool Us and has served as a consultant on magic and the occult to numerous film and television productions.Since 2022, Aiden has also founded the 501c3 Humanitarian Aid Charity Organization Trident Aid, which provides critical medical supplies to the front lines of Ukraine. All of Aiden’s performance proceeds are donated to this organization and cause.

events.title: Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre w/ The Nutcracker
events.description: Unwrap the Magic!Terrence S. Orr’s beloved version of The Nutcracker returns for its final year at Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre, inviting Pittsburgh audiences to gather one last time around this treasured holiday tradition. The Nutcracker overflows with warmth, nostalgia and theatrical magic. As we prepare for an all-new production in 2027, this fond farewell honors a sparkling world that has lived in the city’s heart for more than twenty years.​Set in turn-of-the-century Pittsburgh, Orr’s The Nutcracker whisks audiences into an unforgettable adventure with Marie and the Nutcracker Prince as they journey through swirling snow and into the Land of Enchantment. There, they meet the Sugar Plum Fairy and hundreds of colorful characters, all brought to life with amazing dancing and the iconic Tchaikovsky score.Concept & Choreography: Terrence S. Orr I Music: P.I. Tchaikovsky

events.title: Gwar with Midnight, Mac Sabbath and X-Cops
events.description: GWAR is a legendary heavy metal band known for outrageous theatrical performances, elaborate sci-fi costumes, and shock-rock stage shows filled with satire, horror, and over-the-top spectacle. Their music blends thrash metal, punk, hardcore, and heavy metal influences with dark humor, aggressive riffs, and chaotic live energy. GWAR concerts are famous for immersive visual effects, fictional storylines, and outrageous audience interaction that have made the band one of the most unique acts in heavy music history. With decades of cult popularity and an uncompromising artistic identity, GWAR remains an iconic force in theatrical metal entertainment.Midnight is a blackened speed metal band recognized for raw aggression, fast-paced riffs, and a gritty sound inspired by classic heavy metal, punk, and extreme underground music. Their music combines high-speed intensity, snarling vocals, and old-school metal attitude into relentless songs driven by chaos and rebellion. Midnight has earned a loyal following through energetic live performances and a stripped-down approach that captures the spirit of vintage extreme metal.Mac Sabbath is a parody metal band known for combining fast-food satire with Black Sabbath-inspired heavy metal music and theatrical comedy performances. Dressed in exaggerated fast-food-themed costumes, the group delivers humorous reimagined versions of classic metal songs while creating a bizarre and highly entertaining stage production. Their concerts blend comedy, heavy riffs, and absurd visual storytelling into a unique live experience that has gained cult popularity among metal and comedy fans alike.X-Cops is a hardcore and thrash crossover band built around a satirical law-enforcement theme, featuring aggressive metal riffs, humorous storytelling, and over-the-top stage personas. Known for blending heavy music with comedic performance elements, the group delivers chaotic live shows driven by punk energy and theatrical intensity. Their music combines hardcore aggression with tongue-in-cheek humor that appeals strongly to fans of underground metal and parody-driven performance art.

events.title: Death From Above 1979
events.description: Death From Above 1979 is a Canadian rock duo known for its explosive fusion of dance-punk, noise rock, garage rock, and electronic influences. Consisting of bassist and vocalist Jesse F. Keeler and drummer-vocalist Sebastien Grainger, the band creates a massive sound using an unconventional bass-and-drums lineup that delivers both heavy riffs and infectious grooves. Their music combines raw energy, distorted bass lines, driving rhythms, and danceable hooks, resulting in a style that is both aggressive and irresistibly rhythmic. Renowned for high-intensity live performances and a pioneering role in the dance-punk revival of the early 2000s, Death From Above 1979 remains one of the most distinctive and influential acts in alternative rock.

events.title: THE OLD ALLEGHENY COUNTY JAIL AND MUSEUM-FREE
events.description: Open on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of the month except on Court holidays.Visit at your convenience between 11:30 am and 1:00 pm--Cost: FREEPHLF docents are on hand to tell you the story of the former Allegheny County Jail. Completed in 1886 to the designs of Boston architect H.H. Richardson, it closed on July 27, 1995. The building was then renovated between 1995 and 2001 and adapted for a new use as the Family Division of the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas. Working with the leadership of Allegheny County and with funding from the Drue Heinz Trust, our organization coordinated with the former jail's Deputy Warden Ed Urban and the Allegheny County Juvenile Court to preserve one portion of the cell blocks of the historic jail to create the Old Allegheny County Jail Museum. The Jail Museum, located in Downtown--at 440 Ross Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15219--opened in 2005.To access the Museum: Enter the Family Court Building through the main entrance on Ross Street. You will then be processed through a security checkpoint. The Museum is located across from the vending machine room. The use of cameras is NOT permitted.

events.title: Over the Rhine
events.description: Over the Rhine is an Ohio-based folk-rock duo known for intimate, atmospheric songwriting shaped by Karin Bergquist’s expressive vocals and Linford Detweiler’s piano-led arrangements. Their music blends folk, rock, Americana, and gospel influences, creating performances that feel both reflective and warmly communal. This Pittsburgh appearance, billed as An Acoustic Christmas with Over The Rhine, brings a seasonal dimension to the duo’s richly textured sound. The group’s current work continues to revisit hymns and gospel songs, connecting their long recording history with a reverent, contemporary sensibility.

events.title: Dax
events.description: Dax is a rapper, singer, and songwriter known for emotionally direct lyrics, intense delivery, and a style that blends hip-hop, spoken word, and melodic rap. His music often explores mental health, faith, personal struggle, ambition, and self-reflection through confessional storytelling and dramatic vocal performances. Dax gained widespread attention through viral videos and independently released songs that showcase his lyrical focus and raw emotional energy. With a growing fanbase and a sound rooted in motivation, vulnerability, and personal honesty, Dax has become a distinctive voice in contemporary independent hip-hop.

events.title: Straight No Chaser
events.description: Straight No Chaser is a renowned a cappella vocal group celebrated for its flawless harmonies, inventive arrangements, and infectious sense of humor that have made it one of the most successful vocal ensembles in the world. Originally formed at Indiana University, the group rose to international fame after a viral performance introduced millions of viewers to its unique ability to blend pop, jazz, holiday classics, rock, country, and contemporary hits without the use of instruments. Their performances showcase remarkable vocal precision, clever mashups, and engaging choreography, creating a concert experience that is equal parts musical excellence and lighthearted entertainment. Whether performing festive holiday favorites or imaginative reinterpretations of well-known songs, Straight No Chaser consistently captivates audiences with its polished musicianship, charismatic stage presence, and effortless chemistry. With multiple chart-topping albums, extensive international touring, and a reputation for delivering unforgettable live shows, Straight No Chaser continues to redefine what is possible in contemporary a cappella music.

events.title: Sensory Friendly Time
events.description: Explore the National Aviary during a sensory-inclusive experience, designed for those with sensory processing needs to make the most of their trip. During Sensory Friendly time, you can see and touch biofacts, including eggs and feathers, and enjoy a sensory-friendly version of Passport to Parks, presented by AAA Travel at 11 am. Plus, visit our sensory table and explore our Interactive Play Spaces, including a larger-than-life Draw Alive station. Sensory Bags from KultureCity, featuring items like headphones and fidget toys, are available to borrow daily at the National Aviary.A helpful sensory guide to the sights, sounds, and climate of the Aviary's habitats can be viewed in advance AND during your trip. Please register in advance!

events.title: WILD PINK
events.description: WILD PINK with support from HIDING PLACES $20 ADV / $25 DOS 7PM DOORS / 8PM MUSIC ALL AGES for fans of... This is Lorelei, Ratboys, MJ Lenderman, Waxahatchee BIO: There’s a novelistic impression to the songs of Wild Pink, where characters peer over the edge of potential futures, past mistakes and paths not taken. Backed by a dive bar hue, NYC-based frontman John Ross blends the existential with the celestial, gathering pieces of passer-bys, fictional figures, and historical idiosyncrasies to make sense of what’s in front of him. It’s on their sixth album, Still Coming Down, that Ross cements the voice he’s been steadily honing over the years. The album pokes fun at the listlessness of consumerism, coping through detachment and finding the punchline of it all. Ross is a consummate of curiosity, becoming a narrator of a warped and unpredictable America, morphing everyday mundanity into a cinematic, sepia-toned flipbook. Propelled by the witty and ravenous wisdom of 2024’s Dulling the Horns, Ross’ poetic form has only gained traction, as jocular, heartfelt stories pour with a clever and distinctive ease. NFL bros cruise alongside big guys in grocery stores with even bigger tattoos; ghost stories and references from the cinematic haze of movies like Heat, Moneyball and The Town buzz in the background while Ross also points to Waterworld and The Perfect Storm––heroes who wander, looking for answers at the end of the world. After battling––and beating––cancer, and now becoming a father for the first time, Ross’ outlook has hairpin-bent its way into a simpler significance, where creating music is less about the bigger picture, and more about being present in the moment. It’s a genuine rock record, leaning into the dynamics of open-armed arrangements, inviting huge chords, harmonicas, horns, keys and pedal steel to morph and blend into a cathartic swirl. Ross looked back to the grunge bands he was obsessed with as a teen, and found that it sparked a deeper presence with his own voice, both in lyrics and performance. He endeavoured to create an album that is as fun to play live as it is for the audience to witness, harkening back to the enthusiasm and motivation he felt growing up. “Strangely, I feel like I've found my voice on this record,” he says. Still Coming Down was recorded in one week in Asheville, NC at the renowned Drop of Sun studios with producer and engineer Alex Farrar (Bnny, Wednesday, Samia). Vocal takes were done in two to three bursts, marking a less laborious process than previous records. “There was not a ton of overthinking,” Ross says. He invited friends to collaborate throughout, mimicking the carousel of characters that comes with living a life on the road. Longtime Wild Pink member Dan Keegan lends his percussive talents, with Meg Duffy (Hand Habits), MJ Lenderman and Lenderman’s The Wind bandmates Landon George and Xandy Chelmis adding a raucous vigor to the arrangements. On opener “Box Store” Ross is that college buddy lamenting the empty desires of folks strolling the strip mall and the irony of AC units blocking the view during one of the year’s best seasons. Hearty keys and groaning steel are teamed with electric plucks, piecing together a bursting introduction. “500 is in the New 250” bounces between scuzzy guitars and softer, reflective moments, portraying the push-and-pull of cacophonous rock clubs and the long, quiet drive to the next hotel, bandmates silently staring into their phones. The sauntering “Still Coming Down” captures Ross’ ability to pinpoint some of the more painful parts of life with an eye on a more hopeful horizon. All’s not lost despite the darkness, as Ross relays “I used to be pure / I just try to be good now,” over Duffy’s guitar and George’s fiddle. “Round of Applause At The End Of The World” points to the whirlpools of conspiracy theories and the cloud of misinformation that can take over entire communities. “I don’t know what my idea of fun is anymore,” Ross calls, wry and weary, as distorted guitars respond resolute. The song ends abruptly, like a person you can’t convince otherwise. Still Coming Down is a storied expedition that welcomes in the drifters and the kids kicking up dust; the brokenhearted and the cursed; the ones looking for an answer and the ones who simply couldn’t care less. Ross gives movement to the characters in our heads, the faces we see every few years and the ones who pass us by. It’s proper rock meant to be played loud, with your hand out the car window, riding the air as you bound down some highway in the early hours. Forming soon-to-be-classics that soak in their ability to impact without unnecessary frills, Still Coming Down is about the very nature of songwriting and instinct, learning to trust the process and staying open to the lessons you might learn along the way.

events.title: KING TUFF + SHEER MAG
events.description: KING TUFF + SHEER MAG with support tba $25 ADV / $28 DOS 7PM DOORS / 8PM MUSIC ALL AGES for fans of... Ty Segall, Shannon and the Clams, Screaming Females KING TUFF BIO: There are times in our life when we feel magic in the air. When new love arrives, or we find ourselves lost in a moment of creation with others who share our vision. A sense that: this is who I want to be. This is what I want to share. It’s a fleeting feeling and one that Kyle Thomas, the singer-songwriter who records and performs as King Tuff, found himself longing for in the spring of 2020. But knowing he couldn’t simply recreate this time in his life at will, Thomas—who hails from Brattleboro, Vermont—set out to write a love letter to those cherished moments of inspiration and to the small town that formed him. The one where he first nurtured his songwriting impulses, bouncing ideas off other like-minded artists. The kind of place where the changing of the seasons always delivered a sense of perspective and fresh artistic inspiration. Where he felt a deeper connection with nature and sense of community that had once been so close at hand. “I wanted to make an album to remind myself that life is magical,” he reflects. And so, Thomas seized upon his memories, creating what he calls “an album about love and nature and youth.” The result is Smalltown Stardust, a spiritual, tender and ultimately joyous record that might come as a shock to those with only a passing knowledge of the artist’s back catalog. On Smalltown Stardust, Thomas takes us on his journey to a place where past and present collide, where he can be a dreamer in love with all that he sees. Images of his youth abound: from Route 91 which runs through his hometown (in “Smalltown Stardust”); to Redtooth, a spectre who used to roam the streets (“Bandits Of Blue Sky”); to old friends, old haunts and old dreams (“Always Find Me”); to Vermont’s Rock River, which gave its name to a song of a torch still burning for past love: “Those days are gone and we can’t rewind/ Cuz people grow and places change/ But my love for you will never fade away.” But at the core of Smalltown Stardust is Thomas’s desire to commune with nature on a spiritual level. Images of the natural world, from blizzards to green mountains to cloudy days, fill the songs and create a setting unmistakably far away from Los Angeles. “I consider nature to be my religion,” he explains, and Smalltown Stardust is nothing if not a spiritual exploration. Thomas’s identification as a sort of eternal spiritual seeker is underscored in one of the album’s sweetest moments, “A Meditation,” which features a home audio recording of Thomas as an eight year old, trying his hand at leading a meditation. It’s a journey that he continues to this day, as he intones on “Portrait of God”: “Walking in the woods, wading in the river” and “breathing in the mountain air” before heading back to a place where he finds himself “Oil painting in my garage/Let my colors flow/ I’m working on my portrait of God.” While so much of Smalltown Stardust invokes idealized traces and places of Thomas’s past, the album’s recording process made his communal vision a reality. Thomas’s Los Angeles home in2020formed a micro-scene of sorts, with housemates Meg Duffy (Hand Habits) and Sasami Ashworth recording their own heralded albums (2021’s Fun House and 2022’s Squeeze, respectively) at the same time. A shared spirit dominated an era spent largely on the premises, with Thomas serving as engineer and contributor to both records, and Ashworth working as co-producer on Smalltown Stardust. Thomas describes the time with a fitting metaphor: “I’ve always thrived around other people making things. You want to bloom with each other.”Ashworth’s contributions are vital to the album: she co-wrote a majority of the record and contributed vocals, arrangements, and instrumentation to each song. As Thomas notes, “I tried to follow her vision a lot. It helps to open your world to collaborators. You always get something completely different than you would have expected.” With the gorgeous orchestral tones of “Love Letter to Plants,” it’s immediately clear that Thomas is declaring a wider vision of what his music can be. Gone are many of the squalling guitars of previous King Tuff records, replaced with thoughtful, tender touches of cello and violin on “LoveLetter to Plants,” “Pebbles In A Stream” and “The Bandits Of Blue Sky”; a plaintive saxophoneon “Always Find Me”; and orchestral vocal harmonies with Ashworth that lift the songs to acelestial plane. (Though the rollicking, joyous leads on “Portrait of God” show Thomas hasn’t lost his touch on guitar.) On “How I Love,” Thomas makes clear that all of this is by design: “So lost in nothing but noise for so many years, I forgot to love.” In the end, Smalltown Stardust is not merely a nostalgia trip. In making the record, Thomas not only conjured a special time in his life, he found new inspiration, surrounded by a small circle of collaborators and a sense of love and wonder for nature. If the first King Tuff record was content to merely state Thomas was no longer dead, Smalltown Stardust is a paean to what that life means. A statement of belief and a hymnal to the magic still to behold all around us. “I’m a different person now than I was 20 years ago when I first started it. But oddly, when I first started the band, it was more like this,” he says. Which is to say, things have come full circle. Or as Thomas intones on “The Wheel”: “Ooh we were just kids then… Caught up in the turning of the wheel…. And it’s coming ‘round again.” SHEER MAG BIO: Underlying every great record, every career-defining work of art, is a certain ineffable, increasingly rarified quality: unity of vision. Great songs need not announce their greatness: their marriage of idea with action, soul with sound, appears as something which is naturally effortless, unforced—they are what they are because they have no choice but to be. On Playing Favorites, Sheer Mag’s third full length and first with Third Man Records, this precise, matured clarity of vision is put on full display. Over the course of the past decade, Sheer Mag have labored to carve out a discernibly singular position within the canon of contemporary rock: toggling with ease between the refined flourishes of a “connoisseur’s band” and the ecstatic colloquialism of populist songwriting—yet displaying no strict loyalty to either camp—their sound, while oft-referenced, is unmistakably and immediately recognizable as theirs alone. With Playing Favorites, Sheer Mag have capitalized on a decade’s worth of devotion to their own collective spirit—a spirit refined in both the sweaty trenches of punk warehouses and the larger-than-life glamour of concert halls—emerging with a dense work of gripping emotions, massive hooks, and masterfully constructed power-pop anthems. This is the record the Philadelphian rock and roll four-piece has always been destined to make. Playing Favorites expands with a sense of undeniable vitality, buoyed by rock and roll’s singular capacity to channel a relentless compassion for human life. While at times marked by an intensified sense of melancholy, this newest offering takes stock of the confusing flow of daily life without moralizing, refusing to fall into antagonistic cynicism. Sheer Mag leans into the chaotic thrall of city living, of a life subdivided by the jagged highs and lows of bars, parties, and nightlife culture, with sweetly empathetic remove. The chemically-saturated swing of disco rhythms, crooning earnestness of heartland Americana, and boisterous theatrics of capital-G-and-M Guitar Music become strangely familiar bedfellows. This music is complex, not complicated. As lead guitarist Kyle Seely puts it, “I don’t believe people should put on a record and have to work to enjoy it.” Sheer Mag neither pander towards the studied pretensions of the rock historian elite nor dilute their approach into something more blankly palatable to a commercial audience. Instead, they have their eyes set on that ever elusive third option: those who just get it. If you build it, they will come. Sheer Mag began to work in earnest on their follow up to 2019’s A Distant Call in the summer of 2021, which they originally imagined would take the shape of a tautly constructed 4-song disco EP. As Matt Palmer, the band’s rhythm guitarist and primary lyricist, recollects: “those first four songs came out of a hard moment in life for all of us collectively—they kind of felt like an attempt to figure out how to have fun when you actually feel miserable.” Before long, the band realized this new material would perhaps be better served within the context of a fully fleshed out rock LP, bracketed by the support of a wider array of juxtaposing psychic moods and sonic textures. Over a six-month stretch spanning the fall of 2022 to the winter of 2023, Kyle Seely and his brother Hart Seely (bass) set about tracking the instrumentals for the record, resetting their studio configuration each week in order to impose a more tailored, multi-session atmosphere upon the record’s acoustic landscape. Palmer rejoined vocalist Tina Halladay in Philadelphia the following spring to write and record the vocals for Playing Favorites, which depart rather markedly from the band’s prior material, placing an added emphasis on pronouncedly existential, interpersonal storytelling and ornate background harmonies. Reflecting upon the shift between this newest LP and the band’s previous material, Halladay notes: “those first few records felt like a personal coming out party; they felt like they were an introduction to me and my life story. With these new songs, I feel like I’m finally able to move past that—there are parts on this record that I couldn’t imagine being able to sing ten, five, or even three years ago.” Playing Favorites burns with a sweetened gratitude for the lot one has been given in life: the luck of coming up punk; the luck of living an unalienated life; the luck of feeling love, and losing love. The title track announces itself with a sense of self-assured swagger, spinning a jubilant tale of life on the road: the band is back together, and they know they’ve never sounded quite this good before. A clamoring gust of socially lubricated bravado weaves its way throughout much of the record, such as on “All Lined Up,” which paints images of late nights (early mornings?) spent amongst possible friends, cigarettes fizzing in the ashtrays and a sense of looming dread curling through the air. Every coin has two sides, of course: the candor of Playing Favorites’ sweeter moments is often balanced by a certain studied sadness, that soft grief of living that negatively lends such brighter moments their seductive allure. “Golden Hour” conjures a softly elegiac longing, evoking images of old photographs which shimmer like the fields of Elysium; “When You Get Back” croons about fantasies of a loving future which may never come. Sheer Mag have broken significant musical ground with Playing Favorites, elevating their signature approach to rock and roll to lushly cinematic new heights. “Moonstruck,” for instance, lives up to its titular reference of Hollywood-sized surprise romance, spooling out a charming story of desire crossing the liquid boundary that separates innocent crush from deepening love. Playing Favorites’ filmic qualities reach their peak on “Mechanical Garden,” which lurches forth like a three-part fugue, carrying the listener from ripping glam theatrics into a subtly psychedelic, string and drum machine dub interlude, finally resolving upon perhaps the most openly depressive iteration of Sheer Mag’s take on disco-inflected pop, outfitted with a guest guitar solo by Mdou Moctar. The baroque elegance of such moments find their natural counterpoint in the record’s more straightforward power-pop tracks, such as “Don’t Come Looking,” which courses with the chest-filling bravado of a lightly southern-fried Nerves hit, and “Paper Time,” which delivers a type of mad-dash snare-roll catharsis that brings to mind all of the giddy melodrama of the final heist in a Cassavetes movie. Playing Favorites’ greatest achievement, however, is perhaps its unabashed embrace of nakedly emotional, arena-sized choruses, which seem to fizz out of some sort of timeless radio set to the frequency of pure human experience. As Halladay puts it, “Nobody seems to write straight up rock bangers anymore–more than anything else, we want this record to put huge, catchy songwriting front and center.” Playing Favorites is undoubtedly a record by the same Sheer Mag that audiences of all stripes have spent the last decade falling in love with. In fact, for all of its sonic departures and evolutions, this record is perhaps the most “Sheer Mag” release yet. Not so much a return to form, but rather a realization of those greatest promises that the band has up until now only hinted at. With Playing Favorites, Sheer Mag cater to their tastes and their tastes alone: so long as they continue to do so, the future of rock and roll, that great human tradition, is in the best of hands.

When new love arrives, or we find ourselves lost in a moment of creation with others who share our vision. A sense that: this is who I want to be. This is what I want to share. It’s a fleeting feeling and one that Kyle Thomas, the singer-songwriter who records and performs as King Tuff, found himself longing for in the spring of 2020. But knowing he couldn’t simply recreate this time in his life at will, Thomas—who hails from Brattleboro, Vermont—set out to write a love letter to those cherished moments of inspiration and to the small town that formed him. The one where he first nurtured his songwriting impulses, bouncing ideas off other like-minded artists. The kind of place where the changing of the seasons always delivered a sense of perspective and fresh artistic inspiration. Where he felt a deeper connection with nature and sense of community that had once been so close at hand. “I wanted to make an album to remind myself that life is magical,” he reflects. And so, Thomas seized upon his memories, creating what he calls “an album about love and nature and youth.” The result is Smalltown Stardust, a spiritual, tender and ultimately joyous record that might come as a shock to those with only a passing knowledge of the artist’s back catalog. events.title: Kyle Gordon
events.description: Kyle Gordon is a comedian, musician, writer, and digital creator who has built a large online following through his clever character work, satirical songs, and sharp observations about internet culture and everyday life. His comedy often parodies specific musical styles, nostalgic pop-culture trends, and exaggerated personalities, combining polished production with intentionally over-the-top performances that have become widely shared across social media platforms. In addition to creating viral comedy videos, Gordon has expanded his career into live performances where he blends stand-up, original music, and theatrical storytelling into an interactive entertainment experience. His ability to faithfully recreate the sounds and aesthetics of different musical eras while adding humorous twists has earned praise from audiences who appreciate both the craftsmanship and the comedy behind his work. As his fan base continues to grow, Kyle Gordon has established himself as one of the most inventive comedic performers of the digital era, seamlessly bridging online entertainment and live stage performance.

events.title: Silverstein w/ Story of the Year
events.description: Silverstein and Story of the Year co-headline the Camp Screamo Tour, bringing a high-energy alternative rock and post-hardcore bill to Pittsburgh. The lineup also features Australian pop-punk group Stand Atlantic and Chicago-based alternative rock band Footballhead, creating a diverse night of emotionally charged anthems, driving guitars, and dynamic live performance. With two influential scene veterans sharing the top of the bill, the concert offers fans a rare opportunity to experience Silverstein and Story of the Year together, supported by two newer-generation acts. It is an appealing showcase for listeners drawn to emo, screamo, pop-punk, and modern post-hardcore.

events.title: Joomchi Paper with Rae Gold
events.description: Learn the ancient art of Joomchi, making laminated sheets of mulberry paper into a new sheet of paper. Date: Saturday, December 12, 2026 Time: 10am-1pm Description: We will learn the ancient art of making laminated sheets of mulberry paper into a new sheet of paper that can be used as is or can be part of collage, mixed media, or three dimensional work. Students will leave with a completed piece. Tuition: $65 + $25 materials fee We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Please fill out the application here! You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Materials: All materials will be provided. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Papers Studio, which is on the first floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Paper Studio from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 8 stairs to attend One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. The Paper Studio is located down the hallway from this entrance. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call (and leave a message for) Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Rae Gold has a BFA from Carnegie Institute of Technology (now Carnegie Mellon University). She created one of a kin wearables for 30 years, showing and selling at ACC Baltimore Craft Show, Philadelphia Museuem of Art Craft Show, Smithsonian Craft Show, and Washington Craft Show, among others. For the last ten years she has been creating three dimensional wet felted sculptures, two and three dimensional Joomchi work, and now playing with natural basketry forms.

events.description: Throw a shuttle like the Weave-a-Thon pros! Drop on in and weave a towel! We did the set up for you! Yes, absolute beginners welcome! DROP IN STYLE: 3-hour session! Date: Saturday, December 12! Time: Start times vary: 10 AM, 12PM, 2PM (and expect to stay for about 3 hours after your start time for your towel to reach completion!). You will select your start time when you register. Description: Weaving Curious? This is your chance!!! Absolute beginner drop-in style weaving has arrived! Throw a shuttle like the Weave-a-Thon pros! You, too, can make your very own towel! Come on in and weave on pre-dressed looms! Our team of Weave Coaches will prepare your looms before you get here! All, you will need to do is choose some yarn colors and throw a shuttle. And…..not to worry! our Weave Coaches will guide you through the process, offering tips for throwing those shuttles back and forth to build a special and custom towel of your very own design. What’s more, we will help you take the weaving off of the loom and finish and hem your towel before you leave the studio! You can expect your towel to be about 16 x 20 inches (and it will shrink after washing to about 14 x 18), so as a dear weaver once said these will be “towel-ish” sized, and all a bit different. A sweet hand towel to gift to a loved one or to brighten up your own room! This is a completely beginners welcome offering. No experience expected. There are different beginning time slots to choose. Plan to spend about 3 hours from your chosen start time. For this special holiday edition: Five weavers will be able to begin at each starting time; call up all of your best pals and have a SUPER FUN time together! This is offering is part of our Gift Guide suite of workshops, in which you get to learn something and make a gift for someone special at the same time! events.title: Magnolia Boulevard w/ Madison Hughes
events.description: Doors 7PM | Show 8PM$15 ADV | $20 DOS21+With a southern rock tinged flavor of soulful americana, and a powerful female vocalist reminiscent of Tedeschi Trucks Band, Magnolia Boulevard has blossomed through devastation since forming in 2017. They pushed through the turmoil of COVID-19 that devastated the music industry, the sorrow following the death of their beloved drummer, and the joys of welcoming Maggies daughter into the world. Much like the band members of Magnolia Boulevard have endured the highs and lows of the past few years, so has their music. The bands emphatic and empowering anthems of love, self-discovery, grief, and uncertainty serve as a lesson to us all about lifes unpredictable nature and how to better live in the moment so we can appreciate everything and everyone around us before theyre gone.If patience is a virtue, then the current state of Magnolia Boulevard plays right into the long-held notion that sonic grandeur evolves in its own time and place one where the Lexington, Kentucky, rock-n-soul act is aiming to break into a national audience ready and roaring for the quintets soaring talents.Formed in 2017 by Noelle and Allen, the band came together when other creative endeavors werent fulfilling the artistic desires and professional expectations of what the duo were envisioning. It was time to push down the gas pedal on the possibility and potential of what Magnolia Boulevard could be, and ultimately has become in sonic design and in the live realm.The sound has been described as Appalachian Soul, and I really like that because of our Appalachian roots, Noelle says. You get a taste of folk with the songwriting portion, but you also have that rock and soul foundation. Madison Hughes will make you feel like someone finally said the thing out loud. Not loudly. She doesnt need to be. Her voice carries the kind of weight that sneaks up on you, warm and unhurried, until a single line stops you mid-drive and you sit in the parking lot a little longer than you planned.She grew up in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida, idyllic by every measure, rooted in the same coastal Southern soil that gave the world Lynyrd Skynyrd, Tom Petty, the Allman Brothers, Tedeschi Trucks Band, and Ray Charles. Music was in the air before it was ever a choice. Her fathers folk-rock records: Springsteen, Jackson Browne, Bonnie Raitt, Sheryl Crow, Gillian Welch. Her mothers soft devastation: Dido, Sarah McLachlan, the Cranberries, Norah Jones. The grit and the tenderness both took root.She started writing songs in high school because heartbreak cracked her open and she couldnt say the hard things any other way. That instinct never left. Her sound refuses to sit still, grunge-folk grit threaded through country soul, blues-pop hooks bleeding into indie Americana, all of it held together by feel rather than formula. In high school she was the girl who sat with everyone at lunch, allergic to the idea that you had to pick a side. Thats still who she is. The genre-crossing isnt a strategy. Its just her nature.

events.title: Weave Your Own Towel with the CC Weave Coaches: Holiday Special!
events.description: Throw a shuttle like the Weave-a-Thon pros! Drop on in and weave a towel! We did the set up for you! Yes, absolute beginners welcome! DROP IN STYLE: 3-hour session! Date: Saturday, December 19! Time: Start times vary: 10 AM, 12PM, 2PM (and expect to stay for about 3 hours after your start time for your towel to reach completion!). You will select your start time when you register. Description: Weaving Curious? This is your chance!!! Absolute beginner drop-in style weaving has arrived! Throw a shuttle like the Weave-a-Thon pros! You, too, can make your very own towel! Come on in and weave on pre-dressed looms! Our team of Weave Coaches will prepare your looms before you get here! events.title: THE OLD ALLEGHENY COUNTY JAIL AND MUSEUM-FREE
events.description: Open on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of the month except on Court holidays.Visit at your convenience between 11:30 am and 1:00 pm--Cost: FREEPHLF docents are on hand to tell you the story of the former Allegheny County Jail. Completed in 1886 to the designs of Boston architect H.H. Richardson, it closed on July 27, 1995. The building was then renovated between 1995 and 2001 and adapted for a new use as the Family Division of the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas. Working with the leadership of Allegheny County and with funding from the Drue Heinz Trust, our organization coordinated with the former jail's Deputy Warden Ed Urban and the Allegheny County Juvenile Court to preserve one portion of the cell blocks of the historic jail to create the Old Allegheny County Jail Museum. The Jail Museum, located in Downtown--at 440 Ross Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15219--opened in 2005.To access the Museum: Enter the Family Court Building through the main entrance on Ross Street. You will then be processed through a security checkpoint. The Museum is located across from the vending machine room. The use of cameras is NOT permitted.

events.title: Maybe Happy Ending (Touring)
events.description: Maybe Happy Ending is a tender, original musical romance about Oliver and Claire, two retired Helperbots who find connection, adventure and possibly love in a futuristic Seoul. Blending intimate storytelling, jazz-inflected music and inventive theatrical design, the production explores what it means to be human—even when its central characters are not. Winner of six Tony Awards, including Best Musical, the show is led by Tony Award-winning director Michael Arden, with music and book by Will Aronson and Hue Park. Pittsburgh audiences will experience the production as part of its first North American tour.

events.title: Needle Felting: Bird of the Month: Red Breasted Nuthatch with Erin Carlson
events.description: January (2027)’s bird of the month: Red Breasted Nuthatchl! Learn to needle felt, while enjoying a detailed look at this fascinating bird! 3-hour workshop Date: Thursday, January 7, 2027 Time: 6pm-9pm Description: Learn to needle felt or sharpen your skills while creating your own Red Breasted Nuthatch . Fiber artist and backyard bird enthusiast Erin Carlson of Red Cottage Fiber Studio will guide you through the needle felting process as you look closely to observe the shape and markings of the species and gain a deeper appreciation of our avian neighbors. Adventurous beginners welcome. Please note that we will be using sharp needles and repetitive, detailed hand motions. About the 2026-27 Bird of the Month Needle Felting Series : Due to popular demand, Contemporary Craft is thrilled to once again partner with instructor Erin Carlson to offer this series of workshops! While first offered virtually during the pandemic, this year will be live and in-person! Classes will occur the first Thursday of each month from 6-9pm and run from March 2026-February 2027. Join us for as many classes as you like. Choose your favorite bird or join us for all 12 to complete your very own flock. The bird selections are as follows: March: American Robin April: Scarlet Tanager May: Barn Swallow June: Eastern Bluebird July: Ruby-Throated Hummingbird August: American Goldfinch September: Downy Woodpecker October: Barn Owl November: Chickadee December: Northern Cardinal January(2027): Red Breasted Nuthatch February(2027): Red Winged Blackbird Tuition: $65 + $10 materials fee (per workshop) (if you are viewing this listing on your phone, scroll down to the bottom of the page for the class registration link) Materials: all materials are included. Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Scholarship application is found at this link . You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, TImmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the Fibers Loft on the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. About the Artist Erin Carlson is a multidiscplinary fiber artist working and teaching in th Pittsburgh area for the last decade. She loves to help students explore their creativity through the use of fibers.
